title: Lewandowski and De Bruyne shine in Nations League while Džeko plays his last international game
description: Veteran stars took center stage in the Nations League on Friday with Robert Lewandowski and Kevin de Bruyne leading Poland and Belgium to victories thanks to multi-goal performances.Italy also kept Zinedine Zidane from winning in his home debut as France coach, while Edin Džeko made his last international appearance.
fullText:
Veteran stars took center stage in the Nations League on Friday with Robert Lewandowski and Kevin de Bruyne leading Poland and Belgium to victories thanks to multi-goal performances.

Italy also kept Zinedine Zidane from winning in his home debut as France coach, while Edin Džeko made his last international appearance.

De Bruyne showed he can still dominate a match at age 35 when he scored Belgium's first two goals in a 3-0 win over Turkey in League A.

De Bruyne opened the scoring 10 minutes into the game in Liege when he played a one-two with Dodi Lukébakio and struck from near the edge of the area.

The Napoli playmaker curled home another goal with half an hour to play. Substitute Romelu Lukaku sealed the win over the Turks. Lukébakio hit the post twice.

"I try to lead by example for the younger players, and they follow easily," De Bruyne said. "I feel I can still contribute. I am enjoying myself, and that is the main thing."

Belgium made it two wins and a loss — which came to France — under new coach Mark van Bommel.

When Zidane's name was read out by the stadium announcer after the teams were announced, a roar filled Stade de France.

Things looked good for the home side when Michael Olise put France ahead in the 55th minute with a curling shot from 20 meters which went in off the crossbar.

But poor defending midway through the second half allowed Italy central defender Alessandro Bastoni to run through and clip a low shot inside the right post to secure a 1-1 draw.

France leads Group 1 with seven points, followed by Belgium with six, Italy with four and Turkey with zero.

Lewandowski scored a hat trick to lead a 6-0 demolition of 10-man Romania in League B.

The 38-year-old Chicago Fire striker earned and converted a 24-minute penalty when Romania defender Radu Dragusin was sent off for fouling him in the box.

Lewandowski made it 2-0 in the 47th from a pass by Nicola Zalewski and then rounded off the lopsided victory late with his third goal.

Edin Džeko finished his nearly 20-year-international career for Bosnia-Herzegovina in a 1-1 draw with Sweden also in League B.

Džeko, 40, debuted for his nation in June 2007. He finished with 152 appearances and 73 goals, making him the record holder in both categories for the tiny Balkan nation after helping it reach two World Cups.

Džeko was given an honor guard when he was subbed off in the 63rd, shortly after Viktor Gyökeres scored for Sweden. Kerim Alajbegović equalized in the 80th for the hosts.

Also in League B, Northern Ireland beat Ukraine 3-0 in Slovakia with Ciaron Brown scoring twice.

title: USC legend Taylor Mays returning to Coliseum as coach with Washington
description: When the Huskies visit the Coliseum on Saturday, they will do so with a legendary Trojan on their coaching staff
fullText:
Saturday's football game against Washington will mark Homecoming at USC. Ironically, it will also be a homecoming of sorts for a member of the Huskies' coaching staff.

Washington's safeties coach is a name that should be very familiar to USC fans. Who is it, you ask? Why, none other than legendary Trojans safety Taylor Mays.

Mays had one of the most decorated careers of any player to ever suit up for the Trojans. A four-year starter at safety, he was named a first-team All-American in 2007, 2008, and 2009. Known for his hard hits, Mays finished his time in Cardinal and Gold with 276 total tackles, nine passes defended, five interceptions, and a forced fumble.

Since the conclusion of his NFL career, Mays has gotten into coaching. He served as a defensive analyst on Lincoln Riley's USC staff from 2022-2024, before being named the safeties coach at Washington ahead of the 2025 season.

Now, Mays is set to return to the Coliseum as a visitor for the first time. While USC fans still have plenty of love for the legendary safety, they are certainly hoping to see the Trojans' passing game carve up his secondary on Saturday.

title: NFL Hands Lengthy Suspension to 49ers Owner Jed York
description: The NFL has suspended San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York following his arrest for soliciting a prostitute. The post NFL Hands Lengthy Suspension to 49ers Owner Jed York appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The NFL came down hard on San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York on Friday, handing out a punishment following his arrest for soliciting a prostitute in Ohio that will no doubt leave a lasting stain on his legacy and his family's legacy as owners of 1 of the NFL's premier franchises.

"Just in: San Francisco 49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on Friday.

York was arrested on August 23 at the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in East Palestine, Ohio, as part of an online prostitution sting conducted by local authorities.

"Today, the NFL concluded its review, and I accept its decision in full," York said in a prepared statement. "To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one's failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don't take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead."

York has stayed away from the 49ers since his arrest and while the NFL conducted its investigation.

"49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy, the NFL announced today," The Ringer's Tom Pelissero wrote on his official X account on Friday. "During the time the league's investigation has been proceeding, York has stayed away from the 49ers first three regular-season games, as well as from NFL league meetings. Those three missed games are counted toward his suspension, and he may return on Tuesday, Oct. 20."

York's absence through the first 3 games of the 2026 regular season — the 49ers are 3-0 — will count toward the 6-game suspension.

"49ers owner Jed York has been suspended 6 regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy," The 33rd Team's Ari Meirov wrote on his official X account. "York was arrested after allegedly using a prostitution website to arrange a $140 sexual encounter in the summer … York was away from the team for the first 3 games of the season, and as a result that will count toward his 6-game suspension. So today's announcement is really a 3-game publicly known suspension."

title: Another down-to-the-wire Yankees' decision on Aaron Judge's playoff status
description: Yankees captain Aaron Judge has been hitting against live pitching leading up to Saturday's AL Division Series opener. He has been on the injured list since Sept. 17, due to a right calf strain.
fullText:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – With their spring training and minor league headquarters located across Tampa Bay, there's an at-home element for the Yankees here, too.

So, Aaron Judge made use of Steinbrenner Field in Tampa before participating in Friday's team workout at Tropicana Field.

Judge also hit against live pitching Thursday at Yankee Stadium, in hopes of being added to the AL Division Series roster against the AL East champion Rays.

"We'll see,'' manager Aaron Boone said Friday of Judge's status for best-of-five series, beginning Saturday night.

These Yankees are either facing another playoff round without Judge, or with a limited Judge, due to a moderate right calf strain suffered in a Sept. 16 game.

And they've already made an offensive impression, outscoring the Red Sox, 18-2, in a two-game sweep of the AL Wild Card Series at the Stadium.

Neither Judge nor Giancarlo Stanton – available on the bench as a pinch-hitter – took a swing against the Sox, but the Rays represent their greatest challenge toward claiming a second AL pennant in three years.

The captain also hadn't run the bases since his injury (through Thursday), but "they replicate things in other ways,'' said Boone. "The trainers will obviously play a big part in this.''

Judge might not be an option as a right fielder until next Wednesday, at the extreme minimum, when the series shifts to the Bronx.

The artificial surface at the Trop "plays into it a little bit, just as far as him in the field, potentially'' Boone said of the Judge decision.

"It's more (about) is he going to be available at some point in this series, potentially, as a player? That's what we're kind of weighing and then seeing where he's at now…having taken live BP.

"We'll see how (Friday) goes.''

Boone wasn't yet sure if the Yanks would be taking 10, 11 or 12 pitchers into the ALDS, which impacts the available players off his bench.

It's difficult to imagine both Stanton and Judge on the ALDS roster, in limited capacity. Of Stanton's ALDS status, Boone would only say: "We haven't decided that yet.''

Stanton made that cut for the Wild Card Series, activated for the first time since late April, due to a calf strain (and then two additional calf strains).

"To see velocity and try to visualize yourself out there,'' are Stanton's keys to Judge ramping up to playoff-level pitching, following a layoff.

Judge only had 24 September plate appearances in seven games, after missing 84 team games due to a fractured first right rib.

Personally, Stanton said it's "always good'' to get at-bats, but "I preferred to get two wins and be here now,'' on the eve of an ALDS.

"I'm just trying to win a championship now,'' Stanton said of that elusive prize in his 17th MLB season. "That's what's most important.''

Before the Wild Card Series, Judge, 34, brought up the "very short window'' to achieve his championship aim.

The captain also mentioned earlier how "this team has picked up the slack'' in his absence, and that was before the Wild Card sweep.

Boone said he expected that Ryan Weathers would be available, but no decision was made yet on the lefty's addition to the ALDS roster.

Weathers hasn't pitched in a big-league game since late August, due to a left flexor strain.

"I feel super healthy to be on (the roster),'' said Weathers, who a bullpen session Wednesday.

Weathers threw his second live BP to a group that included Stanton, Jose Caballero and Trent Grisham on Monday at the Stadium.

"I felt a lot sharper in the second one. Better location,'' said Weathers, whose challenge was facing "three of the most passive hitters in baseball'' with power.

If Weathers is added, lefty Ryan Yarbrough's roster spot could be in jeopardy.

title: San Diego State faces mumps outbreak before Texas State game: What we know
description: The San Diego State football team is dealing with a mumps outbreak ahead of Saturday's game against Texas State. Here's what to know about the illness.
fullText:
San Diego State football listed 33 players Thursday on its injury report, with 21 being either questionable, doubtful or out. While some are dealing with football-related injuries, at least 14 players have the mumps, with a 15th being a probable case, according to a university bulletin.

The San Diego Union-Tribune reported Sept. 18 that there were three confirmed and two probable cases of the illness. The Union-Tribune then reported Monday that four more SDSU players had been infected.

Texas State is slated to travel to San Diego for its first conference matchup as a Pac-12 program. Here's what to know about how the breakout affects the Texas State Bobcats' Saturday game against the Aztecs.

SDSU running backs Lucky Sutton and Javion Kinnard are out and doubtful, respectively, for Saturday's matchup after suffering injuries against Toledo. Guard Michael Levelle Watkins is out, while the entire tight end room is on the injury report. Head coach Sean Lewis declined to name the players affected by mumps when asked, citing federal privacy laws.

"The football gods have not really favored us with the injury luck," Lewis told reporters Wednesday.

Most recover from mumps within a week to 10 days, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

Dr. T. Ghosh, medical director of San Diego State Student Health Services, said in an email Wednesday that mumps symptoms can develop 12-25 days after exposure. Therefore, the number of players affected could grow by the time the Aztecs release the final injury report ahead of their game against the Bobcats.

The most apparent physical symptoms include puffy cheeks and a tender, swollen jaw. Fever, headache, muscle aches, fatigue, loss of appetite and pain or tenderness near the ears or jaw are other common attributes.

Mumps spreads through respiratory droplets. Sneezing, coughing, sharing utensils and even talking are ways mumps can spread throughout a group.

The SDSU website states that immunization requirements include two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, or laboratory evidence of immunity, subject to approved exemptions.

The Centers of Disease Control and Prevention website says that two vaccine doses are 97% effective against measles and 84% effective against mumps. Vaccinated people can still incur mumps for a variety of reasons, including prolonged exposure to someone with the virus or if an immune system's ability to fight the infection decreases over time.

title: Our first month with an app broke our commenting records
description: It’s been a banger of a month in the comments section
fullText:
A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it.

The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center.

The results so far are encouraging. In fact, it's helped us set a new all-time record for comments this month across all of SB Nation's communities, and I want to thank y'all for that.

I especially want to thank everybody who's been coming in and keeping things lively during the chat and discussion threads. Whether you're in there getting hyped up or going into full doomer mode, we're glad to be able to provide an outlet for you in a moment when staying in community means so much.

One of the most exciting new features is the game chat. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you're not going to find anywhere else.

We also wanted to elevate the community's contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we've set single-day commenting records three different times since the season started.

And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there's an option at the top to do that.

So, one month in, thank you for making us part of your routine. If you haven't checked it out, you can get it for iOs or Android. And if you're not an app user, that's totally fine! We're glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.

Thanks again for locking in with us on the app and continuing to rock with us in general. Now let's keep on having a fun October!

title: How Michael Jordan partied all night, golfed, then smoked Suns
description: Ex-Phoenix Suns player Cedric Ceballos spoke on All The Smoke podcast about facing Michael Jordan in the 1993 NBA Finals.
fullText:
There are many stories told about how NBA legend Michael Jordan's ultra-competitiveness was unmatched, especially in his prime during the early 1990s.

Former Phoenix Suns forward Cedric Ceballos added another anecdote during this appearance on All The Smoke podcast released Thursday, Oct. 1. He recalled how Jordan "outpartied" Charles Barkley in the Phoenix area when the Suns hosted the Chicago Bulls entering Game 2 of the 1993 NBA Finals.

Ceballos recalled how Jordan went with little sleep after his all-nighter and early golf round prior to that game.

He hung out with his friend Barkley, Ceballos and their teammates at former Scottsdale celebrity hotspot Jetz and Stixx, then managed to play an 18-hole round of golf the following morning in the Valley's June heat.

title: Kentucky basketball hosts Big Blue Madness: Live updates from Rupp Arena
description: Big Blue Madness returns to Rupp Arena. Check out live updates from Kentucky women's and men's basketball programs during the annual preseason event.
fullText:
LEXINGTON — Mark Pope is ready for his third Big Blue Madness as Kentucky's men's basketball coach, which takes place tonight at Rupp Arena.

"An event like none other in the world. It sold out in 22 minutes. Lee Anne just got on for fun about 28 minutes after they went on sale," said Pope, referring to his wife, Lee Anne, "and there was a queue of like 23,000 more people waiting to get in."

For context: Rupp Arena's listed capacity is 20,500.

"At some point, I'm going to make a push to build a 120,000-seat arena (where) we can all enjoy Big Blue Madness together," he said. "But until then, we'll do it. It's going to be a spectacular show.

"I'm nervous about some of the things that our guys have planned, but I think they'll survive."

Pope is entering his third season with the Wildcats. He's 46-26 at his alma mater, with back-to-back NCAA Tournament appearances.

Kenny Brooks, head coach of the UK women's hoops program, also is in Year 3 in Lexington. Brooks and the Wildcats are fresh off a run to the Sweet 16. Kentucky's season ended at the hands of fellow SEC school (and Final Four club) Texas.

Fans will get a glimpse at Kentucky's women's and men's hoopers tonight at 7 p.m.

Courier Journal sports reporter Alaina Morris is at Rupp Arena and will have live updates throughout Big Blue Madness — here and on X, formerly known as Twitter — and complete coverage after. You can follow her on X at @alainammorris.

title: Week 5 Open Thread
description: Here is your thread for all non-UW CFB discussion for the week. But first, some highlights of what to watch all weekend. Friday Evening – It’s not the deepest slate of Friday games, but Penn St trying to rebound from their loss to Wisconsin by traveling to a resurgent Northwestern for the opening of Ryan […]
fullText:
Here is your thread for all non-UW CFB discussion for the week. But first, some highlights of what to watch all weekend.

Friday Evening – It's not the deepest slate of Friday games, but Penn St trying to rebound from their loss to Wisconsin by traveling to a resurgent Northwestern for the opening of Ryan Field is a very good game between unranked opponents. The only other P4 game that night features Virginia Tech hosting Pittsburgh, an anomaly of a game between two unraked 4-0 teams.

Saturday Early – #7 Alabama hasn't looked perfect, but they remain undefeated heading into a tough road game against #16 Mississippi St. Georgia also hosts Vanderbilt in another early SEC game. Notre Dame heads to Chapel Hill for another game they should dominate against Bill Belichick's turbulent UNC.

Saturday Midday – #14 Iowa welcoming #5 Ohio St is the biggest game of this middle window. A week after upsetting Michigan, the Hawkeyes get a chance to insert themselves right in the center of the CFP conversation. Also in this slot, #25 Missouri somehow remains in the polls as a pretty heavy underdog against #8 Florida at home. Tennessee welcomes Auburn to Knoxville.

Saturday Evening – If you click away from the Huskies and Trojans, there are some good Big 12 and ACC games to get your attention. #10 BYU heads to TCU and #12 Texas Tech plays at Colorado. Further east, #4 Miami plays a tough road game against Clemson.

title: Will Benson elects free agency from Cincinnati Reds
description: Outfielder Will Benson is no longer in the Reds organization after electing to become a free agent on Oct. 1.
fullText:
Cincinnati Reds outfielder Will Benson opted to become a free agent on Oct. 1 according to the team's transactions log.

Benson was optioned to the Louisville Bats in June and was then designated for assignment on July 4 after the Reds activated Hunter Greene from the 60-day injured list.

Benson played in just 51 games in his fourth season in Cincinnati, hitting .188 with three home runs and six RBIs.

Benson also struggled while at Louisville, batting .205 in 66 games with four home runs and 17 RBIs.

Benson was a first round pick out of high school by Cleveland in 2016. He played in 28 games for Cleveland in 2022 and was traded to the Reds in February 2023 in exchange for Justin Boyd and cash. Cincinnati also sent Steve Hajjar as a player to be named later.

Benson played in 377 games in four years in Cincinnati, hitting .223 with a .305 on-base percentage, 40 home runs, 45 doubles, 121 RBIs and 38 stolen bases.

This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Will Benson elects free agency from Cincinnati Reds

title: Italy claim draw to spoil Zidane’s first home game in charge of France
description: Alessandro Bastoni spoiled Zinedine Zidane’s homecoming as France head coach as Italy earned a 1-1 draw in their Nations League clash in Paris. The Inter Milan centre-back was the surprise scorer as the Stade de France’s welcome for their former star player ended in somewhat muted fashion with centre-back Dayot Upamecano sent off five minutes from the end.
fullText:
Alessandro Bastoni spoiled Zinedine Zidane's homecoming as France head coach as Italy earned a 1-1 draw in their Nations League clash in Paris.

The Inter Milan centre-back was the surprise scorer as the Stade de France's welcome for their former star player ended in somewhat muted fashion with centre-back Dayot Upamecano sent off five minutes from the end.

Zidane was attempting to become just the third France coach to win his first three matches in charge and first since Henri Michel in 1984 to keep three successive clean sheets.

It was all going to plan after Michael Olise's stunning 55th-minute free-kick only for Bastoni to seize on a lapse in concentration from Lucas da Cunha as he pressed the Como midfielder midway inside his own half as France played out from a goal-kick.

Having gained possession, Bastoni charged into the penalty area and guided a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Mike Maignan.

It put a dampener on the return of Zidane for his first international match on home soil since his retirement as a player following his ignominious exit from the 2006 World Cup final after headbutting Italy's Marco Materazzi.

Two 1-0 wins over Belgium and Turkey had ramped up expectations in the Stade de France, with fans unveiling a 'Zizou' mosaic before kick-off, but the first half was a struggle as the visitors created the best chances.

Moise Kean scuffed an early close-range shot which Maignan scrambled across his goalline to keep out, Davide Frattesi had a snapshot deflected wide and from the resulting corner Kean's goal from a shot on the turn was ruled out for offside.

With Kylian Mbappe out with an ankle injury France looked for inspiration from their array of other big-name forwards.

Desire Doue and Ousmane Dembele were denied by a superb double save from Gianluigi Donnarumma just after the interval but it was the other member of the front three who duly delivered.

Olise rifled in a 25-yard free-kick off the underside of the crossbar for his seventh goalscoring match in nine games for club and country.

But Roberto Mancini's side, who bounced back from an opening defeat to Belgium with a 4-1 rout of Turkey, responded positively.

When Adrian clipped a risky pass into Da Cunha, Bastoni pounced to score with apparent ease.

In a frantic finale Donnarumma tipped Rabiot's shot around a post and pulled off a diving save to deny Eduardo Camavinga from distance either side of Kean looping a header against the crossbar before Upamecano was shown a second yellow card for pulling back Kean.

title: Donnarumma: ‘Italy had attitude of a great team’ in 1-1 with France
description: Gianluigi Donnarumma insists ‘not everyone can come here and put in such a good performance’ as Italy’s 1-1 draw in France. ‘This is the attitude of a great team.’The question after the firs...
fullText:
Gianluigi Donnarumma insists 'not everyone can come here and put in such a good performance' as Italy's 1-1 draw in France. 'This is the attitude of a great team.'

The question after the first two Nations League games was wondering which was the real Nazionale, the one that lost 2-0 at home to Belgium, or the side that crushed Turkiye 4-1 in Bursa?

This evening's performance at the Stade de France seemed to give a response, because it was another strong performance showing progress, as Alessandro Bastoni surged forward and robbed Lucas Da Cunha to cancel out the deflected Michael Olise free kick.

It was the first goal conceded by Zinedine Zidane's France since he took charge, and the atmosphere was set up for this to be his celebration, but it was ruined by the Azzurri.

The Italy starting XI against France for the Nations League Matchday 3 in Paris, October 2, 2026 (@azzurri)

"Coming here and putting in such a good performance is not something everyone can do," Donnarumma told Sky Sport Italia.

Of course, this is a familiar city to the goalkeeper, who spent several years at Paris Saint-Germain, winning the Champions League.

"France are a phenomenal team, and even when we had to defend with a low block, we were united, so I really liked that. I was sad after the Belgium game because it hurts me when we lose, but this is the start of a long journey, and I knew we could have a defeat.

"I am very happy with what this team is doing and we came here with a great attitude. Bastoni's goal saw him come forward and attack them in possession, that is the attitude of a great team."

PARIS, FRANCE – OCTOBER 02: Riccardo Calafiori, Pio Esposito and Sebastiano Esposito of Italy looks on alongside teammates before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between France and Italy at Stade de France on October 02, 2026 in Paris, France. (Photo by Pauline Figuet/Getty Images)

The Manchester City goalkeeper had to make seven saves this evening, the third most in an Italy match during his career.

"I am in a good period of form, I feel calm and they were good saves tonight, but I'm happy because I helped the team and it was a wonderful performance from the whole side."

France confirmed that each of their last 12 goals have been scored after the half-time break, but Les Bleus have not kept a clean sheet in their last seven meetings with Italy.

Nicolo Fagioli of Italy and Ousmane Dembele of France compete in the Nations League MD3 (@azzurri)

"The young players must be allowed the opportunity to make mistakes, because that is how you can experience and maturity. We older figures will try to help them, on and off the field, let them realise how important it is to give 100 per cent in every training session."

There is some news ahead of the final game in this run against Turkiye in Bologna on Monday, because Arda Guler was sent off in a 3-0 defeat to Belgium and will therefore be suspended.

title: Former Yale coach Tony Reno, who led the school to 5 Ivy League football championships, dies at 52
description: (AP) — Former Yale football coach Tony Reno, who led the school to five Ivy League championships over 14 seasons, has died, the school announced Friday. Reno resigned as Yale's coach in February because of health reasons and had been on medical leave since the end of last season.
fullText:
NEW HAVEN, Conn. (AP) — Former Yale football coach Tony Reno, who led the school to five Ivy League championships over 14 seasons, has died, the school announced Friday. He was 52.

No cause of death was given. Reno resigned as Yale's coach in February because of health reasons and had been on medical leave since the end of last season.

"Today, we are deeply saddened by the loss of an extraordinary member of the Yale Athletics family," Yale athletic director Victoria Chun said. "Tony Reno devoted his life to serving others and approached every day with humility, compassion, and purpose. He believed deeply in the power of mentorship and invested wholeheartedly in the success and well-being of his players, colleagues, and friends."

Reno went 83-49 during his tenure, finishing second in the program in career victories behind Carm Cozza, who was 179-119-5. Under Reno, Yale defeated archrival Harvard seven of the past nine meetings.

Reno is survived by his wife, Toni, and their children, Dante, Angelina and Vince.

Dante Reno quarterbacked the Bulldogs to a 9-3 record and the Ivy League championship last season. Playing in its first postseason game, Yale came back from a 42-14 deficit in the third quarter to defeat Youngstown State 43-42. Eventual FCS championMontana State defeated Yale 21-13 in the next round.

The Bulldogs finished 13th in the FCS rankings.

"While his accomplishments on the football field were remarkable, it is the relationships he built and the lives he changed that will define his enduring legacy," Chun said. "Our thoughts are with Toni, Dante, Angelina, Vince, and the entire Reno family during this time."

McKinley has a record of 28-6 against Hoover. The Bulldogs have won four consecutive games against the Vikings and 16 of the last 18 overall. The last win for Hoover in the series came in 2021 (24-0).

McKinley has earned at least a share of the Federal League title 12 times since joining the league in 2012. The Bulldogs have an active streak four-year streak of capturing at least a share of the league title.

Hoover has won 23 Federal League titles since 1968, the most of any program in league history. The last Federal League title for the Vikings came the last time they beat the Bulldogs in 2021.

Brian Baum, North Canton Hoover: Baum enters his 12th year as head coach of North Canton Hoover. He has a career record of 71-53. Hoover has a string of six consecutive playoff appearances currently. He was also named the Federal League Coach of the Year and was the Northeast Inland District Division II Coach of the Year that season. title: Analytics experts weigh in on Colorado's upset chance vs. Texas Tech
description: Analytics experts are skeptical about Colorado's chances against No. 10 Texas Tech in this weekend's Big 12 matchup in Boulder.
fullText:
Colorado faces its toughest challenge of the season so far with the No. 10 Texas Tech Red Raiders coming to Boulder for a Saturday evening matchup.

After back-to-back losses, including dropping their Big 12 opener to Baylor, most people are down on the Buffs and rightfully so. The analytics community is especially concerned with the Buffaloes' past two performances.

ESPN's Bill Connelly listed Texas Tech as one of his top-15 teams on upset alert, but it didn't spark much confidence that Colorado could actually pull it off.

"The Buffaloes' defense has become far more aggressive and disruptive and can challenge a Tech offense that boasts strong efficiency numbers (15th in success rate) but doesn't make loads of big plays, turns the ball over too much and is dealing with O-line injuries...Only one half of the matchup is intriguing, however -- there's little reason to think the Buffaloes will actually score.. It will take serious Boulder magic for this to become interesting." - Connelly

Clearly, Connelly thinks it is at least a possibility that Colorado beats Texas, but nearly everything would have to go right.

Diving deeper into the analytics, SP+ projects the Red Raiders to win by 21 points while ESPN's Football Power Index has Texas Tech winning by 16.1 points. Based purely on the numbers, Colorado has little business being even close to Texas Tech, but as Connelly points out, the Buffs' defense versus the Red Raiders' offense is a matchup to exploit.

title: ‘Stop throwing a pity party’: Brady Quinn rips Deshaun Watson for acting like a victim
description: The Cleveland Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday night, improving the team to 3-1 on the season. The Browns’ early-season success has been one of the biggest surprises in the NFL this year, and it is in large part thanks to the massively improved play from veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson. The FOX Sports…
fullText:
The Cleveland Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday night, improving the team to 3-1 on the season. The Browns' early-season success has been one of the biggest surprises in the NFL this year, and it is in large part thanks to the massively improved play from veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson.

The FOX Sports Radio morning show, 2 Pros and a Cup of Joe, hosted by Brady Quinn, LaVar Arrington, and Jonas Knox, discussed the story surrounding the Browns on Friday morning.

"Credit due, hat off to (head coach Todd Monken)," Arrington said. "He has the Cleveland Browns at 3-1 after a divisional opponent in the Pittsburgh Steelers, who were coming off of a big victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. So give them credit. But I think this is honestly, potentially, this is more of an indictment on the Pittsburgh Steelers than it is a feel-good story for the Cleveland Browns.

“STOP throwing a pity party for what’s happened in the past for yourself. You won a game; make it about everyone besides YOU because, quite frankly, you’re on a really good team!”

– @Brady_Quinn on the Deshaun Watson PR spin. pic.twitter.com/Wab9BaPcmy

— FOX Sports Radio (@FoxSportsRadio) October 2, 2026

"I don't understand this need for a, well, feel-good story," Knox said. "I don't get it. What were the struggles? Let's just like break down the struggles. The struggles were: you had a fetish with the handhouse, and you weren't available. And then when you were available to play after suspension, you were injured. And then when you weren't injured, you were bad."

Quinn went on to make it clear that while he's happy for Browns' fans, he doesn't see why Deshaun Watson is throwing a "pity party" for himself.

"I feel good for the Cleveland fans. Yes. I feel good for a lot of those players," Quinn said. "I'm not sure what PR spin they're trying to put on or revisionist history they're trying to make. Anything that he endured in the past, he brought on himself. I mean, there's, there's not one part of the adversity he faced that he should have been solely responsible for.

"So like, here's the unfortunate part is we have— we're going to keep talking about this because they're going to keep bringing it up and we're going to have to keep addressing it, acknowledging it. Like, dude, stop throwing a pity party. For what's happened in the past for yourself. All right, you won a game, make it about the team, make it about everyone besides you, because quite frankly, you're on a really good team and it is about everyone besides you.

"Like, you're the quarterback, all right? This isn't Lamar Jackson in college running around carrying Louisville or at times carrying Baltimore. Like, you are there because— and you're being successful because of the help you have around you. So I just, I hope he stops with keep trying to get people to feel bad for him."

The Browns and Watson will next face the New York Jets.

title: Former Yale football coach Tony Reno dies after stepping down for health
description: Former Yale football coach Tony Reno died on Friday, the university announced. Reno stepped down in February for health reasons.
fullText:
Former Yale football coach Tony Reno died on Friday, Oct. 2, the university announced.

Reno had stepped down from leading the Bulldogs' program in February for health reasons.

"Today, we are deeply saddened by the loss of an extraordinary member of the Yale Athletics family," Yale athletic director Victoria M. Chun said in a statement. "Tony Reno devoted his life to serving others and approached every day with humility, compassion, and purpose.

"He believed deeply in the power of mentorship and invested wholeheartedly in the success and well-being of his players, colleagues, and friends. While his accomplishments on the football field were remarkable, it is the relationships he built and the lives he changed that will define his enduring legacy. Our thoughts are with Toni, Dante, Angelina, Vince, and the entire Reno family during this time."

COLLEGE FOOTBALL WEEK 5 PREVIEW: Picks for Top 25 games, including SEC, Big Ten showdowns

Reno spent over a decade leading the Bulldogs and transforming them into one of the Ivy League's top programs. Over the course of his decade-plus tenure, Yale went 83-49 overall under Reno, the second-most wins by a head coach in program history.

The Bulldogs won five Ivy League championship titles under Reno in 2017, 2019, 2022, 2023 and 2025. Yale also won seven of its last nine meetings against Harvard in the historic rivalry game series.

Last season, Reno helped Yale secure the conference's first automatic berth to the NCAA Division I FCS Playoffs, where the Bulldogs advanced to the second round after a 43-42 comeback victory over Youngstown State in the first round. Yale finished the season ranked 13th in the country with a 9-3 overall record.

BOLD PREDICTIONS: Florida, Tennessee lead Week 5 upset picks

"Tony was a man who valued the important things in life. Family always came first, and that was evident in the special family he built and the love the Reno family shares," Yale football coach Kevin Cahill, who served on Reno's coaching staff in New Haven for 10 seasons before becoming his offensive coordinator, said in a statement.

"As a coach, Tony loved his players and held them to a standard they often didn't know they were capable of reaching. He was hard on them and demanding, but every day, they knew he cared about them. It was never about him or simply about winning championships; it was about developing young men and leaders and helping them become the best versions of themselves. Along the way, we won a lot of football games. Tony will be missed dearly. His impact on so many lives will never be forgotten, and his legacy will forever be a part of the Yale Football family."

UFC 332 is less than 24 hours away …

It all goes down this weekend (Sat., Oct. 3, 2026), inside Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah. In the main event, the vacant Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Flyweight championship is up for grabs as Natalia Silva collides with Wang Cong.

We have a weekly series at MMAmania.com called "Weekend Lock," where we share one bet that we predict will slap in SLC when the chaotic dust settles. We also want to hear what our readers think (that's you!), so please tell us your most confident UFC 332 betting lock in the comments section below (see full UFC 332 odds here).

Last week's recap: For the second time this year, I've gotten back-to-back weekend locks wrong. At UFC Vegas 121, Mehemmedeli Osmanli's ML did not hit because he got disqualified for a bonehead illegal knee.

Middleweight wrecking machine Ateba Gautier takes a massive step up in competition against longtime division staple Roman Kopylov on UFC 332's main card.

And for once, I'm betting on Gautier not immediately murdering somebody.

This week, I'm locking in Gautier vs. Kopylov Over 1.5 Rounds (-155).

The 24-year-old has finished nine of his 11 professional victories, including four of his five UFC wins. He's enormous for the division, ridiculously powerful and has quickly established himself as one of the most intriguing young Middleweight prospects on the roster.

However, Kopylov represents an enormous step up from everyone Gautier has faced thus far.

The Russian has made 12 walks to the Octagon and, most importantly for this bet, has never been stopped by strikes in his professional career.

Kopylov has five career losses, with three coming by decision and the other two via submission. Nobody has been able to knock him out, and that's especially important considering Gautier's biggest weapon is obviously his devastating striking.

You also don't have to trust Kopylov's chin for 15 minutes.

Kopylov has gone Under 1.5 rounds just once in his entire UFC career, which makes -155 pretty damn nice considering the experience and durability advantage he brings into this matchup.

There's also an interesting dynamic if Gautier doesn't immediately get his opponent out of there.

We've watched Gautier overwhelm opponents with his size, speed, and power, but Kopylov has considerably more high-level experience and has proven he can maintain a dangerous striking output deep into fights. If he absorbs Gautier's early offense, the fight could become significantly more interesting as the younger fighter enters unfamiliar territory.

Gautier's power could absolutely wear Kopylov down and eventually become the first fighter to knock him out.

On the flip side, Kopylov could survive the early storm, force Gautier to work and begin taking over as the fight progresses.

Either scenario works for us as long as the violence holds off for seven-and-a-half minutes.

Well, Gautier could just be that good.

Kopylov has never been knocked out, but durability eventually fails everyone, and Gautier possesses the type of freakish power that can make historical trends meaningless with one clean connection.

There's also always the possibility Kopylov hurts the less-experienced Gautier early, although Gautier has shown no durability concerns thus far.

Still, Kopylov is unquestionably the toughest and most experienced opponent Gautier has faced, and his history suggests he isn't going anywhere easily.

Give me Ateba Gautier vs. Roman Kopylov Over 1.5 Rounds (-155) as this week's "Weekend Lock."

title: Lake vs. Jackson, OHSAA high school football score, live updates

fullText:
JACKSON TWP. — Lake travels to Fife Stadium tonight to face Jackson, and one of these high school football teams is walking out with its first Federal League loss.

The Blue Streaks and Polar Bears own identical 4-2 records, including 2-0 in the Fed. Canton McKinley is the other undefeated team in league play entering the night at 3-0. Kickoff for Lake and Jackson is 7 p.m.

Follow along below for live updates throughout the evening.

Watch Ohio High School Football Live on NFHS Network all year

The Polar Bears won last year's matchup 40-37 and lead the all-time series 20-18. Jackson has won two straight against Lake after the Blue Streaks won the previous two.

The Blue Streaks and Polar Bears go about their business in different ways. Lake hasn't allowed more than 20 points in a game and leans heavily on senior Ty DeGeorge to produce much of its offense. Jackson has scored 34 points or more four times and has a balanced offense that features the Federal League's top passer and top rusher. DeGeorge has rushed for 615 yards, received for 204 yards and scored 12 touchdowns. That includes a 95-yard pick six last week. No other Lake player has more than one TD this season. Jackson quarterback Carter Muhleman has thrown for 1,191 yards and accounted for 18 touchdowns combined throwing and running. RB Chase Mauer has run for 1,029 yards at 6.8 a carry.

Both of these teams feature impact players in the front seven of their defenses. Jackson senior DE Reese Myers leads the area in sacks with 10. He leads the Polar Bears with 53 tackles overall. Junior DE Simon Humphrey leads Lake with 7.5 tackles for loss and two sacks. Senior LB Shannon Billiter has a team-high 43 tackles for the Blue Streaks.

TE Quinn Snyder transferred to Jackson after catching 25 passes for 364 yards and three touchdowns last year for Lake. The 6-foot-4, 210-pound Snyder is coming off his best game as a Polar Bear, with nine receptions for 164 yards and two touchdowns last week vs. Perry.

Both of these special teams units are strong. Lake's Lachlan Baker leads the area in punting at 41.3 yards an attempt. Jackson's Joey Biviano is 19-for-22 on PAT kicks and 8-for-9 on field goals, with a long of 40 yards.

The Blue Streaks have intercepted nine passes this season, led by CB Mitch Wise's three picks. DeGeorge and LB Riley Lovell both have pick sixes.

title: Commanders could be without Terry McLaurin in Week 4 vs Colts in London
description: Commanders star wide receiver Terry McLaurin was a late addition to Friday's final injury report.
fullText:
Just as the Washington Commanders looked set for a Week 4 boost with the returns of linebacker Frankie Luvu and tight end Chig Okonkwo, a last-minute injury could spell trouble on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts.

Star wide receiver Terry McLaurin was added to Washington's final injury report with a hamstring injury. He's listed as questionable for Sunday's game in London.

Losing McLaurin would be a difficult blow for the Commanders, especially this late in the week. Washington's leading wideout had his best game of the season in last week's upset win over Seattle, finishing with six receptions for 77 yards and a touchdown. Through three games this season, McLaurin has 10 receptions for 141 yards and one touchdown.

If McLaurin can't go, someone else would have a bigger role. Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams would be the top receivers, but a player like Treylon Burks, Jaylin Lane, or Luke McCaffrey could receive more time. Some of McLaurin's potential targets could be absorbed by Okonkwo's return and Austin Ekeler's first game back with the Commanders after re-signing earlier this week.

The Colts allow around 255 passing yards per game and rank among the bottom five pass defenses by almost every metric. Washington will have opportunities to move the ball through the air with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota, as Jayden Daniels was ruled out earlier on Friday. This will be the second straight game Daniels has missed.

Another offensive player listed as out for Sunday is running back Rachaad White. He injured his shoulder last week against the Seahawks. White's third-down run late in the game was critical in clinching the win for the Commanders. Ekeler will likely fill White's role.

After missing three games combined in his first two NFL seasons, McLaurin played in all 17 games over the next four seasons. However, a quad injury cost him seven games in 2025, leading to his worst NFL season.

title: Texans get Nico Collins back for Cowboys game, but they won't have Azeez Al-Shaair
description: The Houston Texans got good and bad news on Friday's injury report. Nico Collins is back, but Azeez Al-Shaair is officially ruled out.
fullText:
The Houston Texans are getting their best offensive weapon back this weekend.

Nico Collins, who suffered a hamstring injury two weeks ago in practice, is expected to play Sunday when the Texans host the Cowboys.

He was officially removed from the team's injury report and practiced in full Friday.

Meanwhile, linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was ruled out with a groin injury. Al-Shaair played through the injury in Sunday's loss to the Colts but did not practice this week. Coach DeMeco Ryans said on Wednesday that it's possible Al-Shaair could miss "some time."

Several more players are questionable. They include linebacker Jake Hansen (calf), guard Ed Ingram (groin) and defensive linemen Jadeveon Clowney (knee) and Logan Hall (knee).

The addition of Collins this week is a major development for the Texans, who missed their star receiver sorely. Collins had seven catches for 75 yards and a touchdown in 36-31 loss to the Bills in Week 1. But the Texans scored just 23 points in the two games he missed combined.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

title: Bath gain revenge on Exeter to win 11-try thriller
description: After losing to Exeter at home in the Prem semi-final last season, Bath beat the Chiefs 40-34 in another thriller.
fullText:
Tries: Redpath, van der Linde, du Preez, Russell, Penalty, Hill Cons: Russell 4

Tries: Varney, Yeandle, Iosefa-Scott, Feyi-Waboso 2 Cons: Slade 3 Pen: Skinner

Bath made it two wins out of two in the new Prem season as they gained a degree of revenge for losing to Exeter Chiefs in last season's semi-final.

The two sides produced another thrilling game, just as they did three months ago, exchanging 11 tries as the all-out attack approach to the new season continued.

The hosts scored four tries to have a bonus point in the bag by the break as Cameron Redpath, Bernard van der Linde, Dan du Preez and Finn Russell all scored to put them 26-10 ahead.

Stephen Varney and Jack Yeandle had got Exeter's first-half scores, before Josh Iosefa-Scott and two great tries from England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso turned the match on its head within 15 minutes of the restart.

But Varney gave up a penalty try for a deliberate knock-on and Ted Hill's effort took the game beyond their opponents, although Harvey Skinner kicked a late penalty to ensure the visitors came away from a second consecutive defeat with two bonus points.

The last meeting between the pair at the same venue is a match that will be remembered forever as the Chiefs came from 16 points down at half-time to win their Prem semi-final by a single point.

That defeat dethroned Bath as champions and they were looking ruthless as they grabbed two early tries.

Redpath read Skinner's intentions to make an interception at point-blank range, giving him a free run to the line from inside his own half and there was opportunism about Bath's second score, as scrum-half van der Linde spotted a gap, dummied and sprinted over from just outside the 22.

Exeter had to respond and Feyi-Waboso's burst near the corner drew in enough defenders to allow Varney to exploit space to get his side on the board.

However, they could not keep the hosts out for long with more livewire stuff from van der Linde at the heart of it as he combined with Ewan Richards and although the little South African was held up a few metres short, there was no stopping compatriot du Preez from that distance.

A simple maul from a line-out saw Chiefs hooker Yeandle dot it down for their second try, but Bath had their bonus point on half-time as they worked the ball back to Russell with a bit of space and the Scotland and Lions fly-half did the rest with a dummy, turn of pace and finish.

With Russell converting his own try, it left an identical half-time score to that sunny June afternoon and just as they did three months ago, Rob Baxter's side came storming back and within 15 minutes, they had turned a 16-point deficit into a five-point advantage.

A powerful drive by Kane James punctured a hole in Bath's defence with Iosefa-Scott eventually able to pick and go for the prop's second try in two games.

Then it was Feyi-Waboso's turn to come to the party as he cut a devastating line from outside to in after a huge floated pass from Skinner found him on the touchline.

And his second try arrived thanks to great support play after ex-Bath centre Will Butt danced his way through a gap in midfield to open up the game.

But unlike last time, Bath found a response as their reinforcements from the bench added grunt. Redpath spilled the ball with the line beckoning but as they kept the pressure on, Varney could not resist putting a hand out to stop a pass reaching Joe Cokanasiga and a try in the corner.

The penalty try was awarded and the Italy number nine sin-binned and with a man extra, replacement flanker Hill bulldozed his way to the line and with Russell adding the extras, they had more than a one-score cushion.

Henry Slade missed one penalty to reduce the gap to six points, but Skinner stepped up in the 79th minute from the 40-metre line as Exeter pragmatically made sure they collected a losing bonus point to go with one for scoring four tries, while Bath have a maximum 10 from their two opening wins.

Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter told BBC Radio Devon:

"The important emotion is I'm walking away going 'we've got a team here and we've got something to work with'.

"Last week was such a patchy performance (losing 45-24 to Gloucester) but today we showed a lot of good qualities.

"The qualities of being in a fight to the death, that's what Exeter Chiefs are about. Do you want to be perfect or do you want to be in a fight every single week? Well we'll be in a fight every single week.

"I'm quite happy with that, that's what we're good at and I saw that today."

Bath: Donoghue; Cokanasiga, Lawrence, Redpath, de Glanville; Russell, van der Linde; Obano, Dunn, Stuart, Roux, Ewels (capt), Richards, Pepper, du Preez.

Replacements: Frost, Kirk, Griffin, Hill, Reid, Carr-Smith, Ojomoh, Coetzee.

Exeter: Woodburn; Feyi-Waboso, Slade, Butt, Wyatt; Skinner, Varney; Burger, Yeandle, Iosefa-Scott, Wilson, Jenkins (capt), E Roots, James, Fisilau.

Replacements: Gulley, Goodrick-Clarke, Tchumbadze, Beckerleg, Worley Brady, Wolstenholme, Haydon-Wood, Wimbush.

title: A Cub fan’s guide to the Division Series
description: Sadly, this time without the Cubs
fullText:
Well, that was not the Wild Card round we wanted. This Cubs team provided the highest of highs and the lowest of lows in 2026. We'll think of this as the year of the walkoff, brought to you in no small part by a pitching staff that was decimated by injuries. Pete Crow-Armstrong notching the first 40-40 season in the history of the franchise is clearly the defining highlight of the season, and we'll all celebrate his MVP award when it's official. But at the end of the day this team hit one of their down stretches towards the end of September and really just never turned it around. It's disappointing, but baseball is gonna baseball.

Without the Cubs cheering interest in the Division Series this guide will return to its original vibe: a slightly snarky, but hopefully informative, look at all of the divisional action that kicks off tomorrow in Cleveland. Most of the former Cubs in the field were eliminated in the Wild Card round. So unless you're really pulling for Cody Bellinger and the Yankees for some unfathomable reason, might I propose jumping on the bandwagon of the world's most famous Chicagoan: Pope Leo XIV and cheering for the White Sox?

To cheer for Chicago or to cheer against Chicago? That is a deep question many Cubs fans face today. As a Cubs fan who grew up far away and moved to Chicago in 2015, I've just really never had the animosity for the Sox that many native Chicagoans profess. Cheering for Cleveland, Tampa Bay or San Diego over the Sox really just feels ridiculous. There is no world where I'm taking Atlanta or Milwaukee over a team from Chicago and don't make me laugh by suggesting I cheer for either coastal Death Star, have we met?

The Sox won their first playoff series since 2005 taking out the Astros in Houston. They'll return to Chicago with a flawed, but scrappy team. Manager Will Venable will send Hagen Smith, the Game 1 opener from the Wild Card round, to the mound for Game 1 of the American League Divisional Series. Hey, if it's not broke, don't fix it [VIDEO].

To advance to the American League Championship Series, the Sox will need to thwart the Guardians. The Guardians have won the AL Central for the last three seasons, although they've only posted 90+ wins one time in that period. They'll send Parker Messick, Gavin Williams and (likely) Foster Griffin to the mound.

On the position side Cleveland is still led by José Ramírez, although the future Hall of Famer had a down year this season only slashing .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs with a wRC+ of 92 in 544 plate appearances. To put that in perspective, his 2025 slashline was .283/.360/.503 with 30 home runs and a wRC+ of 133 in 673 plate appearances. Savvy readers will note that 130 plate appearance difference, it seems pretty clear J-Ram was dealing with injuries this year. It's worth keeping an eye on whether the drive all players destined for Cooperstown have will kick in in October transcending whatever issues hamstrung him in 2026. It's worth noting he seemed to tap into that for his 1,000th RBI, which came on this solo home run in September [VIDEO].

The bullpens are closer in raw talent than you might think, with the Guardians rostering one of the best closers in the game in Cade Smith and the White Sox countering with Grant Taylor (who I discussed at length in the Wild Card Series guide). The Guardians relievers put up a 3.54 ERA off a 3.70 FIP with 46 saves in 63 opportunities this season. By fWAR their bullpen ranked second in the American League behind Boston. Meanwhile the White Sox relievers put up a 3.70 ERA off a 4.10 FIP with 41 saves in 71 opportunities. They ranked fifth by fWAR in the AL.

The regular season between these two teams was about as even as it gets with the White Sox holding a 7-6 edge over the course of the season.

The Phillies gave the Braves a real run for their money coming back to win Game 2 of the Wild Card round before ultimately succumbing in Game 3. The Braves won handily, and probably feel a bit of swagger heading to LA. They'll need every ounce of that swagger to take on the defending World Series Champion Dodgers.

There are not probable pitchers announced for either team beyond the Dodgers Game 1 hurler, Tarik Skubal. FanGraphs Roster Resource currently projects Game 1 as a bullpen game for the Braves followed by Chris Sale and Tyler Mahle with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow following Skubal for the Dodgers [VIDEO].

Starting pitching seems like a definitive edge to the Dodgers, if only because L.A. will line up three aces and Atlanta will counter with a future Hall of Fame ace, a solid guy and their bullpen. It's a similar story on the offensive side of the equation where the Braves are led by first baseman Matt Olson who hit 41 home runs in 2026 plus catcher Drake Baldwin, former MVP Ronald Acuña Jr. and Cubs killer Ozzie Albies. But the Dodgers are sporting the second best offense in MLB behind the Chicago Cubs. It turns out even relatively down years from guys like Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman is still utterly dominant relative to the rest of the league [VIDEO].

Even the bullpen, which had given the Dodgers some trouble down the stretch, shows a large edge for LA. While some of their relievers struggled at times this season, they righted the ship in the final two weeks of the season. Closer Tanner Scott had a 2.69 ERA off a 2.10 FIP with 26 saves in 63.2 innings. Braves closer Raisel Iglesias compares favorably to Scott head-to-head with a 2.55 ERA off a 3.17 FIP and 34 saves in 60 innings, however the remainder of Atlanta's pen just isn't in the same league as the Dodgers [VIDEO].

For what it's worth, despite all of the statistical indicators pointing in the direction of the Dodgers, Atlanta won this series handily in 2026 taking five of six meetings between the two teams.

All due apologies to the Tampa Bay Rays with the title here, but until the sabermetrically inclined little front office who could can hoist the Commissioner's Trophy they are going to have to live with looking like the underdog against the Yankees. Yes, that's even true when the Rays won 98 games to their division rival's 93. Yes, even when you've narrowly beaten the Yankees head-to-head in seven of 13 games.

Admittedly, the Rays will likely get a shot at the king playing without their best hitter. Aaron Judge was left off the Wild Card roster due to a calf strain that has kept him from fulling engaging in baseball activities. As of Friday afternoon, it seems probable he'll be left off the Division Series roster as well. Ben Rice did an excellent job filling Judge's size 17 shoes. The Yankees first baseman went five for ten with two home runs and six RBI in the Wild Card round. Meanwhile, the Rays best hitter is absolutely 23-year-old Junior Caminero who hit .276/.360/.524 with 42 home runs and a wRC+ of 142 in 702 plate appearances. Caminero is in the PCA tier of outstanding young MLB talent as evidenced by the fact that it was the second 40-home run campaign of his young career [VIDEO].

The Rays were actually ahead of the Yankees offensively this season, pacing the American League in position player fWAR with the Yankees 2.6 fWAR behind (admittedly, in one fewer game).

The Yankees hold the edge in pitching, however, and you don't need to look further than Cam Schlittler's performance against the Red Sox to see why. While both the Rays and the Yankees have excellent starting and relief pitching the Yankees just edge out the Rays in both categories. While the Rays will send Drew Rasmussen and his 2.67 ERA off a 2.82 FIP in 172 innings to the mound in Game 1 followed by Freddy Peralta and Nick Martinez, the Yankees will counter with Gerrit Cole, followed by Wild Card hero Schlittler and (probably) Max Fried. You can marvel over what a weapon Schlittler can be reliving his 10 strikeouts against the Red Sox below [VIDEO].

The day before the Cubs began their unceremonial march to being swept out of the Wild Card round by the Padres I wrote about my concerns regarding the way they were limping into the Postseason on the back of a difficult schedule. Part of my concern was also how hot the Padres were finishing the season with a 16-2 mark in their last 18 games. Well, now make that an 18-2 mark in their last 20 games as they head into Milwaukee to take on the team who posted the best record in baseball this season: The Brewers.

To be clear, the Brewers aren't exactly limping into the playoffs. They won their last five games and went 15-5 in their last 20. This is truly two teams at their peak colliding. It should be an incredible series for baseball fans.

The Brewers will hand the baseball to likely NL Cy Young award winner Jacob Misiorowski while the Padres will counter with veteran Robbie Ray. Baseball is prone to the strangest outcomes, so it is entirely possible that Ray will outduel Misiorowski just because, however it's hard to fathom they guy who's thrown more than 1,000 pitches over 100 MPH as a starter flopping in early October [VIDEO]:

In game two, Logan Henderson will take on Michael King in a matchup that is sure to give Cubs fans flashbacks to unhittability, and while things are unannounced for Game 3, it certainly seems like a Brewers bullpen situation led by some combination of Dustin May, Shane Drohan and Robert Gasser going toe-to-toe with Nick Pivetta.

The Padres should hold the advantage offensively if they can figure out the Brewers elite pitching. Fair warning, Cubs fans may not like the next video, but I really don't know a better way to show how much damage Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado can do early in the game with the bat than this [VIDEO].

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video.

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video.

The bullpens are probably comparable with maybe a slight edge to the Padres? The question mark is deliberate, it's hard to know how it will play out in reality but the San Diego bullpen can basically shut a game down after the sixth inning with some combination of Mason Miller, Bradgley Rodriguez, Adrian Morejon, Yuki Matsui and Jason Adam. Frankly, that list is deep enough you can imagine it shutting down two games played on back-to-back nights with that crew [VIDEO].

That's no shade to an excellent bullpen in Milwaukee. Trevor Megill, Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby are a fierce trio at the end of games, but you'd absolutely rather be the team wielding the five-headed monster than the three-headed monster to close out games in October.

It's probably more important that both of these teams are the hottest versions of themselves than anything that came before. That said, it is worth noting that the Padres won the season series four games to two.

title: Brown scores two as superb Northern Ireland stun Ukraine
description: Northern Ireland produce one of their best away performances under Michael O'Neill to beat Ukraine 3-0 in Slovakia in the Nations League.
fullText:
Ukraine 0 - 3 Northern Ireland FT

Northern Ireland produced one of their best away performances under manager Michael O'Neill to beat Ukraine 3-0 in Slovakia in the Nations League.

Ciaron Brown opened the scoring with his first international goal and Isaac Price headed home a second in a superb first half for Northern Ireland.

Brown scored his second of the game in bizarre circumstances in the 61st minute when goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk missed his header from the edge of the area and the ball rolled in.

The win maintains Northern Ireland's unbeaten start to the Nations League, and they top Group B2 with two wins and a draw from their three matches.

They can end the opening set of four games unbeaten if they avoid defeat against Georgia at Windsor Park on Monday.

After picking up their first away win in the Nations League in Tbilisi, Jamie Donley and Terry Devlin had half chances as O'Neill's side made a bright start.

The breakthrough came when Kieran Morrison's corner was headed back across goal by Ruairi McConville, and defensive partner Brown reacted quickest to poke the ball over the line.

The visitors' dream start continued with a superb, flowing move, which ended in Morrison's cross being met by Price's powerful header - an 11th international goal for the 23-year-old.

Ukraine, for their part, were restricted to long-range efforts in the opening 45 minutes through Heorhiy Sudakov and Eduard Sarapiy, and captain Trai Hume had an effort blocked by Illia Zabarnyi in the final minute of the half.

Mykola Matviyenko and Sudakov had half chances for Ukraine after the restart but the match was sealed with 29 miutes left when Brown flicked on a free-kick and Riznyk came racing out of his goal but missed the ball, which trickled over the line.

Matviy Ponomarenko's effort was deflected onto the post by Tom Atcheson as Ukraine looked for a response, but three goals and a clean sheet made it a dream night for Northern Ireland.

O'Neill's side are three points clear of Hungary and Ukraine at the top of League B2, while Georgia are bottom on one point.

While the fixture drew recollections and memories of the Euro 2016 finals for fans and the media as the sides met competitively for the first time in 10 years, O'Neill was adamant that his focus was on the future and the new generation of players writing their own history.

That was reflected in his selection as he handed 19-year-old winger Morrison his first competitive start, while the average age of the starting team was just 22 - the youngest for Northern Ireland on record since World War Two.

It was fitting for Brown, the oldest player in the starting XI at 28, to find the opener with his first international goal in the ninth minute.

The Oxford United defender, who has been quietly superb in this international window, managed to poke the ball home off the upright from McConville's knockdown.

Morrison, on loan at Sheffield Wednesday from Liverpool, rewarded O'Neill's faith and was key to the second goal, as he carried the ball forward and played in the cross which allowed Price to score his first goal in more than a year.

But the night belonged to Brown, whose second goal was the slice of luck that had so often avoided Northern Ireland in recent years.

In an convenient nod to Euro 2016, Josh Magennis and Paddy McNair - the only two remaining players from the famous win - came off the bench to see the game out, while 18-year-old Ceadach O'Neill came on for a fourth cap which tied him down to Northern Ireland amid pre-window speculation about his international future.

Sweden and France were the only teams to beat Ukraine in the past 12 months but they had no answer to MIchael O'Neill's side, who were the better team from the first whistle in Trnava.

The win is also NI's biggest away victory since a 4-1 win in Lithuania in September 2021 and marks a third consecutive clean sheet in the campaign.

Northern Ireland will now have the opportunity to go through the international break unbeaten when they host Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's Georgia, who lost 1-0 in Hungary, in Belfast on Monday.

fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The FBI has released a classified report to its workforce examining what it says are chapters from the bureau's history "where this institution fell short," according to an internal message obtained Friday by The Associated Press.

It was unclear what episodes from the FBI's past are chronicled in the new "Patel Report." But the document's existence is in keeping with Director Kash Patel's vocal criticism of the leaders who preceded him and with his determination to rid the FBI of agents he contends have politicized the bureau in the past. Patel's critics say he is the one who has weaponized the FBI and that his scrutiny of his predecessors and their decision-making is part of an effort to rewrite history in favor of President Donald Trump.

Patel pledged at his confirmation hearing last year that he would not look "backward," but as director, he has encouraged investigations of former senior officials and presided over sweeping terminations, including of employees who participated in years-old investigations of Trump, were photographed taking a knee during a 2020 racial justice protest and contributed to a disputed analytical memo about Catholic extremism.

"The Patel Report looks backward because accountability demands it," says a message to the workforce signed by the FBI's co-deputy directors, Christopher Raia and Andrew Bailey. The message describes the report as marking the "closing of one chapter in our history and the beginning of another complete with a brighter future ahead."

Bailey announced his resignation earlier this week, and his last day is Friday. The FBI declined to comment on the report.

The message also says: "We cannot change what happened before we arrived. But we can confront it honestly. We can recognize failures instead of protecting them. We can hold people accountable. We can fix what was broken. And we can build safeguards strong enough to ensure the mistakes of the past are never allowed to define this institution again. These steps are consistent with any institution of excellence that is constantly striving for improvement."

It was unclear if the report made recommendations or demanded any action to address what the FBI now regards as past shortcomings.

The FBI message says the report is meant to "promote fierce organizational accountability" and rebuild "public trust." But Patel's critics say the politically charged investigations into perceived adversaries of Trump that the FBI has embarked on under his watch, as well as the punishment of agents who participated in investigations into the Republican president to which they were assigned, have eroded faith in the nation's premier federal law enforcement agency.

Follow the AP's coverage of the FBI at https://apnews.com/hub/us-federal-bureau-of-investigation.

fullText:
The heatwave is expected to last for nearly a week.

A dangerous, long-duration heatwave is sweeping through much of Southern California beginning Friday, creating increased fire risk in the region.

Extreme to moderate heat warnings are in place for more than 34 million Californians, with temperatures forecast to reach between 92 and over 105 degrees, including along the coastal plains.

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles warned the conditions have created a high risk of "large and fast-moving fires" in the region's valleys and mountains.

The heatwave is expected to begin on Friday and last through at least Oct. 8.

Temperatures are expected to rise to around 15 degrees above average, creating potentially life-threatening conditions for those without access to air conditioning.

Little relief from the heat is forecasted in the overnight hours, though lower humidity is expected.

Windy conditions expected over the weekend will contribute to the fire risk. A wind advisory is in place, with gusts of up to 50 miles per hour forecasted.

Those under heat warnings are advised to watch out for heat-related illnesses, including heat exhaustion and heat stroke.

Anyone experiencing symptoms of heat-related illnesses is encouraged to move to a cooler area, wear loose clothing, sip cool water and apply ice. Those with heat stroke symptoms, including dizziness, confusion or becoming unconscious, are advised to call 911.
