title: The Top 10 Movies Right Now, According to Streaming Data
description: Discover the top 10 most-streamed movies right now—from horror hits like "Backrooms" to family favorites like "Toy Story 5."
fullText:
The most-streamed movies in September, according to JustWatch, include a couple of early Halloween treats: low-budget, high-scare horror flicks Backrooms and Obsession both made the top 10. If you like more gentle supernatural stories, 1990s classic Practical Magic made the charts too. You could also check out best-actor-ever favorites Robert De Niro in The Whisper Man and Dustin Hoffman in Tuner. So there's something for everyone.

Director Kane Parsons' analog horror breakthrough is proof that atmosphere, mood, and a fascinating story is scarier than CGI monsters every time. Based on the viral YouTube series of the same name, Backrooms tells the story of Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor), a store owner who discovers a labyrinthian liminal space in his furniture shop's basement. Renate Reinsve plays his therapist, who thinks it's a delusion, until she goes downstairs for a visit. A hit with critics—Backrooms is sitting at 87% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes—and audiences, Backrooms is a delicious early Halloween treat for horror fans. Stream Backrooms on HBO Max.

Released to streaming to coincide with the sequel's release in theaters, Practical Magic is a beloved supernatural rom-com finding a new audience in 2026. Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman play Sally and Gilly, sister-witches cursed with losing any man they ever love. Sally's romantic interest appears in the form of Aidan Quinn playing a detective investigating the disappearance of Gilly's abusive boyfriend. Can love, magic, and the power of sisterhood break the family curse? With a little help from '90s nostalgia, you bet they can. Stream Practical Magic on HBO Max.

Director Curry Barker is still in his 20s, but his debut theatrical feature is the kind of horror film that changes the entire genre. Obsession is a classic "be careful what you wish for" story that feels fresh thanks to its talented young cast, unpredictable plot, and careful pace. Michael Johnston plays a young man too scared to tell his crush how he feels, so he wishes she'd fall in love with him instead. The result is a nightmare embodied by Inde Navarrette, whose portrayal of the villain/victim is at once harrowing, terrifying, and heartbreaking. Obsession is the best horror movie I've seen in years. Stream Obsession on Peacock.

Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh play Cold War enemies brought together when Reynolds' plane crashes in the Russian wilderness. Branagh is ex-KGB, but he's always been a secret fan of America, so he helps Reynolds escape the USSR. Like the best bro-coms, Mayday is powered by the charisma of its stars, and you won't find any actors alive with more rizz than these two. If you like 1980s-style buddy action/comedies, Mayday is the right stream for you. Stream Mayday on Apple TV+.

In this crowd-pleasing sci-fi flick, Ryan Gosling stars as Ryland Grace, a middle school science teacher who is blasted into the firmament in a last-ditch effort to save the world. Grace is the only person on Earth who might know how to protect the sun from a cosmic infection that threatens all life, but he's definitely not an astronaut and doesn't see himself as a hero either. Will he rise to the occasion and learn something about his inner strength and resilience while saving us all from death? My money is on, "yeah, probably." Stream Project Hail Mary on Prime Video and Fubo.

You shouldn't mess with a superhero's dog. Milly Alcock plays Kara Zor-el, AKA Supergirl, who traverses the galaxy hunting for Krem of the Yellow Hills (played by Matthias Schoenaerts). He shot Krypto the superdog with a poison dart, and justice must be administered. If you want a grittier take on the super-people of Krypton with some deep-lore DC universe building, look no further than Supergirl. Stream Supergirl on HBO Max.

Based on the novel by Alex North, The Whisper Man stars Robert De Niro as Peter Willis, a retired detective who returns to the game to solve a grisly cold case. A copycat is mimicking the crimes of the notorious Whisper Man, a serial killer Willis captured years before. This intense thriller is built around De Niro's powerful performance and a twisty plot that will keep you on the edge of your couch. Stream The Whisper Man on Netflix.

You wouldn't think the life of a piano tuner would be exciting until you see Tuner. Leo Woodall plays Niki White, whose quiet life is turned to 11 when he learns he can use his ears for cracking safes as easily as tuning Steinways. Desperate for cash, White joins up with hardened criminals, and things go haywire. The excellent cast of this smart, tense thriller includes Dustin Hoffman and Havana Rose Liu. If you like suspense in the style of Hitchcock, check out The Tuner. Stream Tuner on Paramount+.

Directed by Jon Favreau, The Mandalorian and Grogu sees Din Djarin (Pedro Pascal) and his adorable baby Yoda pal pitted against Imperial warlords and the Hutt Twins. It's classic Star Wars: a lone hero and his companion doing heroic things while facing impossible odds. Packed with cliff-hanger action and colorful characters, The Mandalorian and Grogu is pure fun in movie form. Stream The Mandalorian and Grogu on Disney+.

Pixar is so good at what it does, it can even make the fifth movie in a series about ratty old toys into art—not just art for kids, but art that's palatable for parents, too. In Toy Story 5, Woody, Buzz, Jessie and the gang face a toy's most terrifying enemy: technology. Toy Story 5 asks if there's a place for action figures and Mr. Potato Head in a world where screens are the only thing kids care about. Stream Toy Story 5 on Disney+.

title: Four Major Issues Are Plaguing the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max
description: Apple's latest iPhones are already going through it.
fullText:
On paper, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are Apple's best smartphones yet. They run the new A20 chip, feature cameras that use a revolutionary variable aperture, and, according to Apple, have the longest battery life of any iPhone ever. And yet, the iPhone 18 Pro's launch has been a rocky one, beset by glitches and hardware issues that range in severity. Some have been fixed by simple software updates, while others remain unresolved.

None of this is to encourage you to return your iPhone 18 Pro or discourage you from buying one if you have your sights set on Apple's newest Pro phones. However, it's important to note that this has hardly been a drama-free rollout. As of this article, these are the four major problems I've seen with the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The first iPhone 18 Pro issue that I saw was random reboots. Users complained that, after a failed Face ID attempt, their iPhones would freeze up and, after a short period of time, reboot. Curiously, Apple's newest Apple Watches, the Series 12 and Ultra 4, had similar reboot issues. While annoying, this was clearly just a glitch with Apple's newest iPhones running iOS 27 and Apple Watches running watchOS 27. The company quickly released patches for all devices in iOS 27.0.1 and watchOS 27.0.1, each of which only mentioned this singular patch in the release notes.

While Apple says iOS 27.0.1 only patches this reboot glitch, AT&T says otherwise. The company sent alerts to iPhone 18 Pro Max users this week urging them to update to this latest version of iOS, warning that iPhone 18 Pro users might not be able to text, call, or connect to data at times, including when dialing 911. The full message reads: "Hi, it's AT&T. Action needed: An important Apple software update for your iPhone 18 Pro Max is available. Some phones may be unable to complete calls/text/data, including to 911. Update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately — Settings > General > Software Update. Please contact AT&T or Apple if you have questions."

As it happens, iPhone 18 Pro users are not included in this alert. As MacRumors speculates, it might have something to do with the iPhone 18 Pro Max's modem. This is the only new iPhone this year to ship with a Qualcomm modem rather than Apple's own C2 modem. As MacRumors notes, affected iPhone 18 Pro Max users can lose service, forcing their phones to drop into SOS mode.

Some iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max users are reporting strange "cracking" or "popping" noises coming from their new smartphones' speakers. This Redditor shared that the sound comes intermittently from the upper speaker, and sounds like someone pulling an aux cable out of a headphone jack. Users in the thread concurred: One user complained of a light buzzing when the volume is set to 100%, while another said their iPhone has a crackling sound when on calls with "mono speaker." According to one Redditor, updating to iOS 27.0.1 didn't fix the issue.

While the thread is full of users complaining of similar issues, not everyone has the same experience. Some Redditors say they haven't heard the sounds on their iPhone 18 Pros, including multiple Mashable reporters. Another user noted that they're experiencing the issue on their iPhone 16 Pro Max since they updated to iOS 27.

As Mashable highlights, some iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max users are noticing that the finish on their devices is starting to wear away, particularly around the camera lens. It seems the majority of the complaints, if not all of them, are from users with burgundy and black iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max devices, and it's not clear how widespread the issue is. Some users have claimed that cleaning the affected area with a Q-tip is enough to fix the issue, while others say the finish itself has worn away.

title: 15 Hacks Every Opera Browser User Should Know
description: If you use Opera to surf the web, you need to know these hacks.
fullText:
The Opera you're using today is obviously a very different browser from the one it was decades ago. Perhaps the most significant change is that it's now a Chromium-based browser, which means you can install Chrome extensions to fill any features you may be missing. That said, the browser still retains its core philosophy of shipping useful integrated features—even if those options aren't always obvious. From bypassing unskippable YouTube ads to using a built-in volume booster for every tab, here are the best Opera hacks you should know about:

If you live on the bleeding edge of tech, you can use Opera's "Early Bird" to try all kinds of experimental features. To do so, click the three-line menu in Opera's toolbar, scroll to the bottom, then select Go to full browser settings. Now, enable Early Bird, go through the list of features on the page, and enable the ones you wish to try. At the time of writing, these features include Browser Connector, which connects the browser to ChatGPT or Claude, and Sharing Point, which adds a button to share an Opera download link with your contacts. Note that these features can change or be removed at any time.

Opera has a sidebar that lets you install "apps" within your browser. It supports ChatGPT, Gemini, Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Translate, WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Bluesky, music streaming services, and a few more apps. These services are pinned to the left pane, and function as their corresponding apps do. You can think of these as pinned tabs in your browser, which are all neatly stacked in the left pane. I've used the sidebar to run Apple Music, a few messenger apps, and Gmail, which is easier to track than the same services in different apps.

Of course, the sidebar versions of these services may not always have all the features that proper desktop apps do (e.g., music downloads on Spotify), but the overall implementation is quite good. Sidebar apps appear in a floating window in Opera, and you can pin that window to the screen if you wish to. You can configure the Opera sidebar by clicking the three-dots button in the bottom-left corner of the screen.

You can open two tabs side by side in Opera for improved multitasking. To start, right-click an inactive tab in the tab bar and select Create split screen. This will place that tab, as well as the active tab, in a split-screen view. I find this helpful for research: For example, you can open a lecture in the main tab, and a search engine, AI service, or a notes app in the second tab. In split-screen view, you can 

Opera supports bypassing unskippable video ads on various sites, including YouTube. When you watch a video in Opera, and an ad starts playing, you'll see a tiny forward button at the top of the video. When you click it, the browser will instantly take you to the end of the ad, though you may still have to press YouTube's "Skip" button. If you're on the ad-free tier of your streaming services, you can stop the Video Skip button from appearing on videos by going to Opera settings > Video. From here, disable Show Video Skip button on all supported videos.

I often watch videos in picture-in-picture (PiP) mode when I'm browsing the web or working, but I get annoyed when I have to keep moving the window around to avoid obscuring text on my screen. Opera has a useful feature to sidestep this issue: It lets you adjust the opacity of PiP windows, and you can make them translucent enough to avoid disturbing your workflow. To enable this for all PiP videos, go to Opera settings > Video, and enable Make pop out transparent. If you'd rather do this manually for each video, start playing the video, then click the pop-out button at the top of the video to send it to PiP mode. Finally, click the Transparency button in the top-left corner of the PiP mode video.

Like most tech companies these days, Opera has a bunch of AI features in its browser. Luckily, you can easily disable most of them. Go to Opera settings > Opera AI, then disable Opera AI and ChatGPT in the sidebar. This also removes the AI button from the browser's toolbar. Finally, you can click the three dots in the bottom-left corner of Opera's window and uncheck ChatGPT and Gemini.

Opera ships with a way to control the volume levels on each tab, a feature that requires an extension on most other browsers. When you're playing media in any tab in Opera, hover your mouse over the corresponding tab, and you'll see a floating menu with a volume slider. This lets you set the volume from 0 all the way to 500%, which can be great for audio sources with low volume levels. You can also use this feature to play music at a lower volume while listening to a lecture or a podcast.

Opera has a hidden enhanced privacy mode, which blocks trackers while you're browsing the web. You can enable this via Chrome Flags: Type opera://flags in the address bar and open the page. Then, use the search bar to look for Enhanced privacy settings section. Use the drop-down menu next to the feature, and select Enabled. Restart Opera, then go to Opera settings > Privacy & security. Scroll to the bottom and enable Enhanced privacy protection. Note that this may break the functionality of some websites, but I've been using it for a few days without any noticeable negative effects.

Opera has a few hidden keyboard shortcuts that tie actions to a single button, instead of the usual two or three key combinations. You can go to Opera settings > Features > Shortcuts, and turn on Enable advanced keyboard shortcuts to use the following keyboard shortcuts:

Press 1 to cycle left through the list of tabs.

Press 2 to cycle right through the list of tabs.

Press / to use the "find on page" feature.

Press 0 (zero) on Windows/Linux or + on Mac to zoom in.

Press 8 to zoom in more (in increments of 100%).

Press 9 on Windows/Linux or - on Mac to zoom out.

Press 7 to zoom out more (in increments of 100%).

Press 6 to return to 100% zoom.

Press Ctrl-` (the tilde button) to go to the previous tab you'd clicked.

Opera has a powerful Snapshot tool you can use to take a screenshot of the visible page, the entire webpage, or save the page as a PDF. I typically ignore all browser screenshot tools in favor of OS options or third-party apps, but Opera's screenshot tool is solid. After capturing a screenshot, the app opens a preview window where you can make basic edits and annotations. To use this tool, click the camera button in the toolbar, then select one of the available options. You can choose Capture visible page to take a snap of the webpage visible on the screen, Capture full page to take a screenshot of the full site without scrolling, or Save page as PDF to save the screenshot as a PDF. You can also take a cropped screenshot as well, if you only want to capture a specific section of the page.

Keyboard shortcuts and mouse gestures are useful, but Opera goes one step further with its "rocker gestures." Rocker gestures let you press the mouse buttons in a particular sequence to go back or forward on any webpage. You can try this by holding the left mouse button, clicking the right mouse button, releasing the left button, then releasing the right button. You can rock from the right button to the left to go back, and from left to right to go forward. To enable rocker gestures, go to Opera settings > Features, and scroll down to the "Shortcuts" section. Here, click the switch next to Enable rocker gestures.

Opera for Android now has an eSIM feature that lets you hop on a cheaper international roaming plan at certain times. If you're unhappy with your provider's roaming plans, you can check out Opera's offering. At the time of writing, Opera offers 3GB of free data for three days. The free data offer is available for people in the U.S., the U.K., Brazil, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Sweden, and the UAE. The roaming plan is currently supported in 47 destinations.

To use this feature, download Opera for Android on a phone running Android 10 or newer. Tap the profile icon in the bottom-right of the browser's home screen, scroll down, and select "eSIM." Hit the "Claim now" button, pick the destination you're visiting, review the plan summary, and tap "Confirm." This will activate the free trial. Opera says you can buy more data once the free plan expires, and that the data plan won't activate until you reach the destination you've selected.

Opera has had a built-in VPN for a few years, but there's now a way to automatically activate the feature when you connect to public wifi networks. That way, you can protect your browsing even if someone takes a peek at the public wifi connections. To use it, go to Opera settings > VPN, and enable "Always use VPN on public Wi-Fi." This feature is currently available in France and the U.S., but Opera says it'll add more regions in the future.

When you select a currency on any webpage in Opera that doesn't match your local medium of exchange, the browser will display the converted currency in a pop-up. However, you don't have to stick with Opera's default currency. If you're traveling abroad, for example, you can change the setting to match the local currency, so you can quickly covert to the currency you'll be paying in. To set this up, go to Opera settings > Search engine, and go to the "Search Pop-up" section. Select the drop-down menu next to "Currencies to", and choose your preferred currency.

Opera also has a built-in webpage translator. The moment you open a webpage in a foreign language, it'll offer to translate the webpage to English. If you speak multiple languages, this can be quite annoying, but it doesn't have to be. You can ask Opera to skip translations for websites in languages you also understand. Go to Opera settings > Languages, and in the "Opera Translate" section, click the Add languages button. You can add multiple languages to this list, and it'll skip translations for all.

title: 'I reduced my running because of urine leaks' – Commonwealth finalist Korir
description: Kenyan runner Naomi Korir was born with fistula, a condition which can cause the uncontrolled leakage of urine or faeces.
fullText:
Naomi Korir's career on the track reached a high point in August when she finished fifth in the final of the mile at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

But things could have been very different for the Kenyan middle-distance runner.

The 28-year-old was born with fistula, a medical condition in which abnormal openings develop between organs and can lead to uncontrolled leakage of urine or faeces.

While Korir loved athletics as a child, it initially forced her to rethink any plans to be a runner.

"I played most of the sports activities: football, netball, athletics, even rugby," she said.

"But it was difficult because [of] the training, and the urine is flowing continuously. It's bad.

"I reduced my running to shorter distances to reduce the leaking.

Despite the challenges, Korir's love of sport also offered a form of escape and belonging.

"I could do it because I loved it," she explained.

"Because most of the people could avoid me, I did a lot of activities just to pass time and not to feel that I'm excluded."

The charity Doctors Without Borders estimates that 500,000 women live with fistula globally.

Some develop a fistula after childbirth while for others, like Korir, it is congenital.

Access to good obstetrics, or to simple surgery, means that the condition has all but disappeared in some countries, but it remains a problem in sub-Saharan Africa, where high quality medical care can be hard to access.

Korir was born with genitourinary tract fistula - an opening between bladder and vagina which caused her urine leakage.

Surgery was required, but her first two operations failed to solve the problem.

In August 2013, a third operation finally brought relief for the then 13-year-old.

The procedure was carried out in her home town Eldoret by the Gynocare Hospital, which specialises in fistula, obstetrics and reproductive health.

"It's a difficult condition to live with every day," Gynocare director Caroline Mabeya told BBC Sport Africa when discussing the stigma and isolation women with the condition suffer.

"They are ostracised in the society. That's the psychological torture that they face with the fistula."

The hospital has treated patients from across East Africa since opening its doors in 2011. Its work extends beyond surgery, with a post-operation programme designed to help women rebuild their confidence.

"We offer free treatment for these women at Gynocare because most of them are very poor," Mabeya explained.

"When they come into the facility, they are crushed, they have low esteem. So, there's a huge amount of effort that is put in to make them at least be strong enough to be reintegrated and get back into the community."

For Korir, successful surgery offered a second chance, both on the track and in the classroom.

As well as allowing her to run properly again, she continued her education through Gynocare's Beyond Fistula programme.

"I have a family in GynoCare, a fistula home," she said.

"That is where I schooled after my surgery until I finished my secondary level."

In 2019, Korir began competing professionally and two years later was part of the Kenyan duo which claimed a silver medal in the 2x2x400m mixed relay alongside her partner Ferguson Rotich at the World Relays in Poland.

A year later she went one better, bagging gold as part of Kenya's 4x400m relay team at the African Championships in Mauritius.

The mile at this year's Commonwealth Games was her first appearance in major global final.

"I'm giving hope to young women maybe who have lost hope," she said of her achievements.

"They need to come back again in living and enjoying life."

Mabeya says Korir's transformation makes her a powerful example to the women currently receiving support at Gynocare.

"She makes them realise that you can actually pull yourself out of these struggles and still make it in life and succeed.

"Naomi actually is one of those patients that inspires us to continue working very hard, because we struggle with this condition and these women. The work is not easy."

As a young girl, Korir sang in church and played the keyboard, convinced that music was a more likely career than athletics.

"But now I'm in different career and I'm so happy," she beamed.

And with the World Championships in Beijing next year and the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, Korir believes there is another chapter to write.

"I know I'm a champion in life, because conquering fistula alone is being a champion.

"Now I'm looking forward to be a champion in sport."

title: Harmison signs first professional Durham deal
description: Charlie Harmison, son of 2005 Ashes winner Steve, signs a two-year deal with Durham.
fullText:
Charlie Harmison, son of 2005 Ashes winner Steve, has signed a two-year deal with Durham.

Harmison, 18, is a fast bowler like his father, who made 63 Test appearances for England between 2002 and 2009.

He is the fourth son of members of the team which won the Ashes urn back after an 18-year wait to sign professional terms with a County Championship club.

Captain Michael Vaughan's son Archie is with Somerset, while all-rounder Andrew Flintoff's sons Rocky and Corey are at Lancashire and Kent respectively.

"I'm buzzing to have signed my first rookie deal," Harmison told the club website., external

"I'm looking forward to the hard work that lies ahead and hopefully contributing to helping the club to success in years to come."

Steve Harmison was part of the Durham side that won the County Championship title in 2008 and 2009 and retired in 2013.

The Chester-le-Street side were promoted back to the top flight this season after winning the Division Two title.

Wicketkeeper-batter Robbie Bowman, 19, and batter Luke Symington, 18, have also signed rookie deals.

title: Homeless to history? Green eyes record-breaking UFC year at 40
description: At 40 years old, UFC lightweight Bobby Green is showing no signs of slowing down as he sets his sights on a historic end to 2026.
fullText:
For all that has changed in the UFC over the past 15 years, Bobby Green has remained one of the promotion's few constants.

Green, 40, has racked up more than 30 fights since making his debut in 2013.

Since then, the American has cemented himself as a fan favourite for his all-action and, at times, slightly wild fighting style and his brash personality.

But almost a decade and a half after he first made the walk to the octagon, Green is belatedly enjoying the finest run of his UFC career.

Green is on a four-fight win streak as he prepares to face Esteban Ribovics at UFC 332 in Salt Lake City on Saturday.

He heads into the lightweight bout with a place in the UFC record books in his sights.

After defeating Lance Gibson Jr by split decision last December, Green has recorded stoppage wins over Daniel Zellhuber, Jeremy Stephens and Terrance McKinney.

Victory over Argentina's Ribovics would make it four wins from as many fights in 2026, leaving him one win away from joining an exclusive group of fighters to record five wins in a calendar year. Yet that appears unlikely to satisfy him.

"I get the business and I understand it. There's nothing wrong with that. But I'm not moving," Green said. "I'm not going anywhere. You're going to keep giving me this money."

There are few sports that contrast the bright lights of fight night with the harsh realities of everyday life more starkly than mixed martial arts, and Green has been reminded of that in the build-up to UFC 332.

In September, fewer than six weeks after pocketing a $100,000 (£75,690) Performance of the Night bonus for his knockout of McKinney at UFC 329, Green revealed he was temporarily without a home and was living out of his car.

The situation was met with widespread confusion from the UFC community, including president Dana White, after Green had previously said he had used his career earnings to acquire a number of properties.

Green has since said he had been left without permanent accommodation after all nine of the other properties were occupied by friends, while a break-up with his partner derailed plans to move into another property.

"So about the homeless thing. I am homeless, but I'm not houseless. I can go to anyone's house," Green said on social media.

"I just don't have my home, and I put everybody else before me, just to make sure all my family was taken care of, my friends were taken care of.

"I can go fight and figure it out, but them, it's gonna be harder for them to figure it out."

After a chaotic couple of months for Green, it is little wonder the octagon has felt more like home than ever before.

Saturday promises to be a pivotal moment that could go some way towards writing the next chapter of Green's storied career.

The veteran is entering the final two fights of his current deal with the UFC and has acknowledged his performance against Ribovics could define what comes next.

After defeating McKinney to match the longest winning streak of his UFC career since 2014 (four fights), Green was keen to be matched against a top-15 opponent in the lightweight division in a bid to reclaim his place in the rankings for the first time since July 2024.

But at 40 years old, Green knows his place in the food chain and accepts he is likely to be used as a yardstick for up-and-coming prospects.

"It's an out-with-the-old, in-with-the-new business," Green said. "Our pay-checks go up, so we've got to get the new guys in to get us guys out of there. Do you know what I mean?

"It's just business. They've got to cut the pay down, keep it to a certain amount. And so if they get rid of some of us guys and make new stars, why not?"

During his media appearances this week, Green made no secret of his dream to one day fight for the symbolic BMF title.

The BMF title is awarded to the 'baddest' fighter in the UFC and has been competed for five times since its inauguration in 2019.

With only a couple of fights left on his deal and currently outside of the rankings, his chances of being matched against the current BMF champion, Charles Oliveira, appear unlikely.

But for someone who has been around the sport long enough to experience his fair share of highs and lows, there is a different dream he is closing in on.

"The focus is changing my family's life and making it a better life," Green said.

"I want to get towards the BMF belt, but at the end of the day, give me my money."

title: Chinese judoka disqualified for alleged bite on opponent
description: Chinese judoka Tang Jing is disqualified from the quarter-finals of the Asian Games with the coach of her opponent claiming that her athlete was left with bite marks on her arm.
fullText:
Chinese judoka Tang Jing was disqualified from the quarter-finals of the Asian Games after appearing to bite the arm of Japanese opponent Rin Maeda.

Tang was disqualified for unsportsmanlike behaviour in the women's -70kg bout in Nagoya, with Maeda progressing and ultimately winning the event.

Having been separated from a hold early in the encounter, Maeda rolled-up her sleeve to show the referee her left forearm, with what appeared to be a bite mark visible just above the wrist.

Officials reviewed video footage before handing three-time Asian Games medallist Tang the disqualification.

"It looked like it was really going to bleed," said Maeda's coach Maki Tsukada.

"We didn't talk about disinfecting it or anything like that, but the bite mark was very clear and distinct."

Tang, 31, appeared to contest the decision before shaking hands with Maeda and leaving the competition area without offering the media interviews.

Maeda, 21, said she was unsure what would happen after she spoke to the referee.

"It's not something that happens very often, so it was a first for me," she told reporters after securing a gold medal with a victory over Kazakhstan's Azhar Askhat.

"I wasn't really sure what would happen myself, but I did tell the referee. I was in a little pain, but once I got on the mat, the adrenaline kicked in and I didn't really notice it, so it was fine."

title: Saracens exile was 'bewildering', says returning Lozowski
description: Sale centre Alex Lozowski says the end of his decade-long stint at Saracens was an anti-climax after being reduced to a fringe player for his farewell campaign.
fullText:
Sale centre Alex Lozowski says the end of his decade-long stint at Saracens was "sad" and "bewildering" after being reduced to a fringe player for his farewell campaign.

The 33-year-old England international made only two Prem appearances for Saracens last season, with a 10-minute Champions Cup cameo off the bench his only game time since the end of February.

"It was a sad ending for everyone I suppose," said Lozowski.

"They finished fifth, which is not where they wanted to be, and I wasn't part of it at all.

"No-one really got what they wanted.

"It was probably just a bit of a damp squib at the end of the season really, which was a shame. It was bewildering and peculiar to me.

"They have their decisions and their reasons and, even though you can disagree with them as strongly as you like, it doesn't really count for much."

Lozowski, whose form in the 2024-25 season won him call-ups to England's squad for both the autumn internationals and Six Nations, was overlooked in favour of a midfield combination of Olly Hartley and Nick Tomkins for Saracens' run-in.

A streak of five successive victories took the London club to the brink of the play-offs before they lost away to Exeter in a semi-final shootout in the final round of the regular season.

"Sport teaches you all kinds of different lessons and now it's like a distant memory, but at the time it sort of stings," added Lozowski, who had a youth trial with Premier League side Arsenal and played for Chelsea's academy before being released and focusing on rugby.

"I've played 198 games, could have got a couple 

Lozowski, who starts in Sale's midfield alongside fellow summer signing Joe Marchant at Saracens on Sunday, admits proving his value to his old club, along with spurring on his new side's season, will be part of his motivation.

"I know Sale wanted me to come here and add value, which meant a lot to me," he said.

Lozowski is not the only member of Sale's travelling party who will be in familiar surroundings at the Stonex Stadium.

Director of rugby Alex Sanderson spent 17 years at Saracens, initially as a player before working as a coach at the club.

Brendan Venter, who has returned to Saracens this season and already been fined for opting out of media appearances, was Sanderson's first boss as a coach.

"I idolised Brendan to a degree," he said.

"A lot of his traits, his values and philosophies I'm aligned with. I've taken from them over the years.

"Not withstanding Mark McCall's unbelievable contribution [who led Saracens for 15 years between Venter's stints], it's good to have him back in the Prem as a character. I'm sure we'll see his character come out on to the field."

Sale are seeking to avenge two heavy defeats against Saracens last season, going down 65-14 away from home in October, before an 85-16 thrashing in April's reverse fixture.

title: Robertson's Scotland career in numbers as 100th cap looms
description: Andy Robertson is poised to become only the second man ever to play 100 times for Scotland. BBC Sport Scotland charts his international career in numbers.
fullText:
Andy Robertson is poised to become only the second man to win 100 caps for Scotland in more than 150 years of international football.

The national captain could hit the century mark in Saturday's Nations League game against North Macedonia as he closes in on the all-time cap record.

A constant presence since Gordon Strachan handed him his debut in 2014 when he was a fresh-faced left-back with Dundee United, Robertson has defined a generation of the Scotland national team.

Here, BBC Scotland charts the Tottenham Hotspur defender's international career in numbers.

Inside the fairytale journey of Scotland captain Robertson

Robertson set to hit 100 Scotland caps - but who else makes top 10?

The great Kenny Dalglish is the only man to have pulled on the navy blue of Scotland more times than Robertson.

'King Kenny' still tops the list on 102 caps, but that could be eclipsed by his friend come November should the 32-year-old feature in each of Scotland's remaining Nations League games this year.

It is fitting that it will be Robertson who surpasses that long-standing milestone, given the pair have forged a friendship over his time with Liverpool.

Not that Dalglish is having that.

"He always says 'you've got millions more games; Nations League, what's that? They didn't have that in my day!'" Robertson joked on the Stick to Football podcast recently.

"I think he might bring up a ratio for years-to-games-played so he's still on top.

"It's obviously something that's been on my radar for a while now. When you get to 80-odd caps, you start to look up."

Dalglish can console himself that his record of 30 goals - held jointly with Denis Law - is safely out of Robertson's reach.

Of current players, John McGinn is lurking only eight behind Robertson on the all-time list, though, so the Scotland men's centurion club could have three members soon.

Since being given the armband by Alex McLeish after Scott Brown retired in 2018, Robertson has captained Scotland 29 times more than any other player.

At the time, he had earned just 22 caps and was just 24 but had established himself as Liverpool's left-back as they reached the Champions League final.

Now, he is the only man to have lead Scotland out at three major finals, reaching the milestone at the World Cup this summer.

Scotland and Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay enthused: "He's such a great captain and he's got that good balance between being one of the senior players and saying you need to wake up if you're not playing well.

"Then he's also got the personable side, organising things with the manager, helping young players and stuff. He's brilliant with that, brilliant."

Robertson has played under four different permanent Scotland team bosses in his 12-year international career.

It was Strachan who plucked him from the under-21s to hand him his debut as a 19-year-old in a win over Poland in March 2014.

McLeish made him captain in 2018, calling Robertson the "outstanding candidate" and an "inspirational figure" - and now he has played twice for new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

He even played one game under interim manager Malky Mackay in a friendly against the Netherlands at Pittodrie in 2017 as the Scottish FA searched for Strachan's replacement.

However, it is Steve Clarke's seven-year stint that Robertson will be mainly associated with, as the pair lead Scotland to three major tournaments.

Robertson played 68 times for Clarke, all of them as captain, and the recently departed head coach consistently praised his figurehead.

"He's been a fantastic captain for Scotland," Clarke said at the World Cup.

"He's worked ever so hard for the country and he leads the group like the leader he is - and he's very, very important to me and the squad."

Given his longevity, it is perhaps no surprise that Robertson also tops the Scotland assist charts since his debut in 2014.

However, Robertson's rampaging runs and crosses from left-back have been pivotal for a Scotland side that has never been free-scoring during his career.

And, although he only has four Scotland goals, there have been a couple of important ones.

His strike against Cyprus helped ensure the Clarke era started with a win in 2019. And his last-minute winner against Poland in 2024 temporarily staved off Nations League relegation.

That was the last time Robertson scored for Scotland.

Over the piece, Robertson's caps are spread fairly evenly among friendlies and qualification games.

Crucially, though, he has also played nine times in major tournaments. What will rankle with him is there is only one win among those nine - June's victory over Haiti in Boston at the World Cup.

Overall, though, Robertson's Scotland career can be characterised by consistency.

He has started 97 of his 99 caps, and played an average of 83 minutes per game, rarely ever being substituted. He has not missed a camp in three years.

The only question seems to be how many Scotland caps will Robertson end up with? At 32 and still playing in the Premier League, it appears there will be plenty more to come.

title: Belfast boxing legend Close dies aged 57
description: Ray Close, the Belfast boxer who almost handed Chris Eubank the first defeat of his career, has died at the age of 57.
fullText:
Ray Close, the Belfast boxer who almost handed Chris Eubank the first defeat of his career, has died at the age of 57.

One of the most gifted boxers Northern Ireland has produced, Close was born in 1969 and turned professional in 1988 after a decorated amateur career.

Close won the EBU super-middleweight title on St Patrick's Day in 1993 but it was his bouts against Eubank for which he will be most remembered.

Eubank, who had won all 35 of his professional bouts, was the defending WBO super-middleweight champion in May 1993 but Close pushed him all the way in Glasgow and the pair could not be separated on the scorecards.

A rematch took place at a raucous King's Hall in Belfast the following year and Close put in another strong performance but lost on a split decision.

A third fight was scheduled to take place but Close's boxing licence was revoked by the British Boxing Board of Control before it could take place after a MRI scan revealed two lesions on his brain.

Close would later return to the ring after obtaining a licence in the USA and he won all five of his bouts in Illinois, the last of which was a knockout victory over Larry Willis in June 1997.

His professional record reads as 25 victories, three defeats and one draw - which came against Eubank.

Ledley Hall Youth and Boxing Club in east Belfast, where Close started his boxing journey as a 10-year-old, led tributes and said he was a "true gentleman, humble, kind and always willing to give something back".

"To our young people, Ray was proof of what could be achieved," the club posted on Facebook.

"He was someone who had come through the same doors, trained in the same club and gone on to accomplish incredible things."

The club added that Close's story has "inspired generations of young people at Ledley Hall and will continue to do so".

"There are some people who become part of the history and heart of a place, and Ray will always be part of ours.

"We will remember him with enormous pride, affection and gratitude."

Bangor Abbey Boxing Academy, where Close had trained, said he will be a "huge loss to the boxing fraternity of Ireland and across the world".

"Ray and his whole family have been a huge part of our club over the years, right from the very start and we are truly devastated."

title: Peterborough appoint Forest Green boss Savage
description: Peterborough United appoint Forest Green Rovers boss Robbie Savage as Luke Williams' successor.
fullText:
Peterborough United have appointed Forest Green Rovers boss Robbie Savage as their new manager.

The 51-year-old replaces Luke Williams at the Weston Homes Stadium after he was sacked on 19 September following a poor start to the League One season which has left Posh 23rd in the division.

Savage played as a midfielder for clubs including Derby County, Birmingham City, Leicester City and Blackburn Rovers.

He guided Forest Green to seventh in the National League last season but they were beaten in the play-off eliminators.

This season they sit 13th after 11 matches, with four wins, three draws and four defeats.

Former Wales international Savage was appointed by Forest Green in July last year, having previously managed fellow non-league side Macclesfield.

He will take charge of Peterborough for the first time when they host Ipswich Town Under-21s in the Jersey Mike's Trophy on 6 October, before Posh resume their league campaign with a trip to his former club Leicester on 10 October.

Savage, who has signed what Posh describe as a "long-term" contract, told the club's website, external he had been attracted to "the size of the club, the philosophy, working with young players and making them better".

He said: "I am really looking forward to getting out there on the training ground, but I am a manager - I will be there for every session, but I believe in trusting the coaches in delivering the messages and the session.

"I am not a manager who is going to want my teams to pass the ball around the back and chalk up 600 passes every game, we are going to go for it and attack and if we are 1-1 at home with five minutes to go, I want my teams to go for the winner.

"I understand there will be people out there with reservations. We all know the modern world has changed with social media. I understand it. I have been around for a long time. I will stand on that touchline and protect my players, it is a brilliant squad, I can't wait to get going, it is going to be fun."

Caretaker boss Ryan Harley will be Savage's assistant.

Chairman Darragh MacAnthony added: "Excitement is the word I can use to describe the appointment of Robbie Savage as our new manager. A word I personally haven't used about our football club for too long.

"His personality, character and mindset is something we need top to bottom. Nobody will work harder to get us up and running again than Robbie. The board were blown away by him in an extensive interview and his hunger to fix our issues and get confidence back into our talented squad is what I am most excited by."

Savage will continue to co-host BBC Radio 5 Live's football phone-in 606, and will be on-air for Sunday's edition from 18:30 BST.

Robbie Savage is an extremely surprising appointment for Peterborough United.

His managerial record to date is modest by League One standards and there are question marks over his ability to handle Darragh MacAnthony's famously hands-on style of ownership.

And yet, following two years of stasis, perhaps a Robbie Savage-shaped curveball is exactly what the Posh need?

Savage inherits a side sitting second from bottom of the League One table.

They have scored only four goals in the league so far this season - and won only two of their past 23 league fixtures stretching back into last season. Key players have been sold and the summer replacements are yet to convince.

Savage will certainly need to hit the ground running. Job security has proved in short supply for recent Posh managers - with the notable exception of Darren Ferguson.

Luke Williams lasted nine months, Grant McCann the same. Steve Evans reached 10 months. Savage clearly has a huge task on his hands, but whatever happens - you get the feeling that it's unlikely to be dull.

title: Timely recognition or long overdue? How Gross is proving all-time bargain
description: Named the Premier League's player of the month for September, BBC Sport looks at Brighton star Pascal Gross' impact both this season and over the past nine years during his two spells at the club.
fullText:
Having been named the top-flight's player of the month for September, it leads to the question of whether Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross may be one of the best value-for-money signings in Premier League history.

In fact the 35-year-old has effectively cost the Seagulls minus £3m - and been involved in 85 Premier League goals over two spells.

Nobody has been involved in more top-flight goals than Gross this season - six in five games.

He was Brighton's first Premier League signing in 2017 for a reported £3m from Ingolstadt and left for his boyhood club Borussia Dortmund in 2024 for £8m.

But in a surprise move he returned to Albion in January for about £1.7m.

Since Gross first joined Brighton nine years ago, only three players have created more chances in the division than his 562 - Bruno Fernandes, Kevin de Bruyne and Mohamed Salah.

And that includes the 18 months he was away from the Premier League.

So has Gross been underrated all this time?

Former England midfielder, and BBC pundit, Danny Murphy doesn't think so.

"The Premier League is shown worldwide, and he has been a part of that for so many years during a time when Brighton have been a shining light," he said.

"You don't have to play for a big-six team to be appreciated in the Premier League. Gross is not under the radar, because people know how good he is."

Gross was Albion's first signing after they sealed promotion to the top flight.

A little-heralded German from relegated Ingolstadt, nobody could have anticipated the impact he, nor Albion, would go on to have.

For one he has played in 73% of their top-flight games since 1983.

"There's an argument Gross is pound-for-pound the best value player in the Premier League over the last 10 years, especially when you look at his goal involvements," said BBC Radio Sussex commentor Johnny Cantor.

"However, he also drives standards in training, sets a high bar and is a huge influence in the dressing room.

"Technically he is excellent, has superb delivery but also possesses an awareness, popping up in spaces all around the pitch. Managers have leaned on him, team-mates respect him, and fans of all generations adore him.

"He will surely be remembered as one of the best Albion players of the modern age."

As well as his notable record of creating chances, Gross has put in more successful crosses, including corners, than any other player in that time (483) despite Trent Alexander-Arnold and James Ward-Prowse attempting more.

For passes played into the box - including those crosses - he is fourth.

Gross also features seventh for assists with 51 to go with his 34 goals in 252 Premier League games.

All the more remarkable when you consider his journey with Brighton appeared over two years ago when he went home to join his beloved Borussia Dortmund.

Albion supporter Maz Mirzadeh said: "When he left for Dortmund, it was like going through a heartbreak and seeing an ex go back to their childhood sweetheart.

"He's outrageously good and massively underappreciated.

"If you watch him play, you would think someone's put him in slow-motion settings, but what he lacks in pace, he makes up in superior football IQ, technical brilliance and working harder than any other player on the pitch."

Follow Brighton & Hove Albion on BBC Sounds

Pre-match, post-match and topical Albion content

Subscribe and listen for everything you love about the Seagulls

Gross played 66 times for Dortmund, scoring one goal and assisting 17 times, but on 2 January 2026, he came back to Brighton.

Aged 34 at the time, many wondered if it was more of a romantic career swansong.

"There may have been concerns that he may not have been able to recreate the impact of his first period at the Amex but that has been dispelled already," added Cantor.

Only Chelsea's Joao Pedro can match Gross' goal contributions this season in the top flight (both three goals, three assists).

Remarkably Gross has run 

The midfielder - who retired from international football after the World Cup - has also played every single minute for Brighton in all competitions, eight games so far.

Former Liverpool and Fulham midfielder Murphy said: "He's an intelligent footballer, with a great football IQ.

"You can see that he has grown into that version of himself over the years. That happens in football - it happened to me - when you know what you can't do, as much as you know what you can do.

"So, you don't see him trying to beat people on the outside with his pace. Instead he loves a little chop, or a Cruyff turn to give himself space and time, or to play a quick first-time pass around the corners. That's why he always seems to be in space.

"His versatility tells you about his intelligence as well. He is able to play as a full-back, central midfield or, recently, as more of a 10. He is scoring and making goals.

"I am sure this won't be his last season with Brighton but, even if it was, he is already going to be remembered as one of the Brighton greats by their supporters for what he has given so far to the club, especially with him coming back and doing what he is doing. It is nothing short of remarkable."

Gross has also created more Premier League chances (15) this season than anyone else to help Brighton to third in the table.

This form led to him being the sixth oldest player to be named Premier League player of the month.

Seagulls fan Mirzadeh added: "Even in his 'unc' era, he's showing the Premier League's elite how it's done.

"If he was called Pascal Silva and played for a top-six club he might get the recognition and respect he truly deserves."

Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan

title: French cyclist Auge in induced coma after crash
description: French cyclist Ronan Auge is placed in a medically induced coma following a crash at the Tour of Langkawi in Malaysia.
fullText:
French cyclist Ronan Auge has been placed in a medically induced coma following a crash at the Tour of Langkawi in Malaysia.

The 22-year-old sustained serious injuries on stage six of the UCI ProSeries event and was taken to hospital.

A statement from his team, Unibet Rose Rockets, described Auge's condition as "currently stable and not life threatening."

Auge's crash is the latest in a series of serious incidents that have marred the sport of road cycling in recent months.

Six riders have died during road races in the past three years, including British cyclist Fin Tarling who was killed in a crash with a vehicle on the UCI Europe tour's Volta a Portugal in August.

American rider Ezra Caudell was hospitalised last month, external with "multi-system trauma" following a crash at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic.

The eight-stage Tour of Langkawi, which forms part of the UCI's second tier tour, is staged on the western side of the Malaysian mainland and concludes on Sunday.

title: Why Aston Villa are playing Sevilla for a trophy you haven't heard of
description: Aston Villa are set to take on Sevilla in the Antonio Puerta Trophy, named in memory of one of the Spanish club's former players.
fullText:
On Friday evening, Aston Villa will walk out at Sevilla's Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan stadium to compete for a piece of silverware that, outside of Spain, few supporters will have heard of, the Antonio Puerta Trophy.

It's a friendly match held in memory of Sevilla academy graduate Antonio Puerta, who died in August 2007 at the age of 22.

Puerta suffered a cardiac arrest during a La Liga match against Getafe and, despite initially appearing to recover and walking to the dressing room, collapsed again and died three days later in hospital.

His death stunned Spanish football. He had been one of Sevilla's own.

Puerta made his first-team debut during the 2003-04 season and went on to make 88 appearances for the club and one for Spain, in 2006.

He helped his team win five trophies in 15 months, including two consecutive Uefa Cups, now known as the Europa League.

A year after his death, Sevilla created a trophy in his honour and what began as a relatively modest pre-season fixture has become an annual part of the club's calendar.

This year's 15th edition of the Antonio Puerta Trophy is particularly interesting because Aston Villa are the first English club to be invited to play for it.

There is also an obvious connection between the two clubs.

Villa boss Unai Emery will return to the stadium where he enjoyed one of the most successful spells of his managerial career.

Emery managed Sevilla between 2013 and 2016, winning the Europa League three times in succession.

Sevilla have won 12 of the previous 14 editions of the trophy, with only Granada and Boca Juniors having managed to beat them in the fixture.

The early editions were all-Spanish affairs, with Sevilla taking on fellow La Liga clubs, before teams from outside the country began to be invited.

Boca Juniors became the first overseas opponent in 2016, followed by Roma, Schalke, Independiente del Valle, Al-Ittihad and Al-Qadsiah.

Villa's Leon Goretzka has travelled to Sevilla after a knee injury so could be available to play.

Striker Brian Madjo is also available after being out since Villa's 2-1 loss to Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup in August, while Taylor Harwood-Bellis will also look to get more minutes.

title: Will Warrington or Wakefield be Super League's sixth winner?
description: Only five clubs have lifted the trophy in a Super League Grand Final - Warrington and Wakefield now have the chance to add their name to that list.
fullText:
Just five sides have lifted the trophy at Old Trafford in a Super League Grand Final.

That exclusive club of Wigan, Leeds, St Helens, Bradford and Hull KR will gain a new member on Saturday as Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity battle under the lights at the Theatre of Dreams for a spot at glory.

Whereas the Super League era has traditionally been dominated by the powerhouses of the sport with their heaving trophy cabinets, 2026 is the story of one side that has come close but not got over the line and another that has upset the odds to wedge themselves into the conversation.

But what is the mood like in either camp ahead of a box office Grand Final?

Wakefield's stunning semi-final win over Wigan set tongues wagging across rugby league and beyond, particularly given the nature of the demolition job delivered by Daryl Powell's side to the treble-chasers.

It was a performance which suggested Wakefield had the credentials to complete the job at Old Trafford, built on a marauding, metre-chomping pack and skilful, pacy backs capable of racking up points.

Head coach Powell has been around the block and knows just how difficult this one-off final is to get right even with a season's worth of momentum behind a team.

"We have to get the same performance level," Powell told BBC Sport. "When it really counts.

"I'm not saying it's going to be picture perfect, it's very rare there is but I think we have to be at a very high level to beat Warrington and we all know that."

'You could be legends' - inside unfancied Wakefield's rapid ascent

Will 2026 finally be Warrington Wolves' year?

Quiz: Name every Super League Grand Finalist

While this is Wakefield's first final and the same for many of their players, like coach Powell a select few have sampled the unique atmosphere of Old Trafford for Super League's showpiece event.

Tom Johnstone begrudgingly left Wakefield for Catalans in 2023 and reached the Grand Final in his first season, before rejoining Trinity in 2025.

That night ended in disappointment with defeat by Wigan, so the 2026 final represents a second chance for the England winger to pick up the ring he so covets - although it will not be the most important ring in his life as he admits.

"It's going to be different in so many ways for me because as much as I loved Catalans, this is my team," Johnstone told BBC Radio 5 live.

"This has been my team for almost all of my career, and the team that gave me an opportunity 15 years ago as a youngster.

"So, this is special, this is the big one and it's probably going to be, if we get it done, the best night of my life. Sorry, after my wedding, my wife said. She said it has to be second to my wedding."

Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final

'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield one win from title

Like Warrington, Wakefield have waited a long time to return to league glory, with a 58-year gap since their last title.

That narrative is one of many utilised by both clubs as inspiration for this Grand Final encounter, with several on both sides.

One story for Wakefield to thrive upon is the impending retirement of stalwart back-rower Jay Pitts.

Born in Ossett and a graduate of the youth set-up at Wakefield, the 36-year-old has amassed just short of 200 appearances for Trinity across two spells bookending his career which will end once Saturday's final is done.

Pitts has battled through this crucial period following a bicep injury, and his determination and leadership are integral to the spirit within the dressing room.

"After the Wigan game I just went into the changing rooms and said to him 'you know you get to play your final game at Old Trafford'. It's what dreams are made of," Powell added.

"While there's a few players leaving us for different reasons, for Pittsy retiring after his final game in rugby league - what better way for us all to do something special for him as a person?

"He's been a phenomenal player, a warrior, and I know all the boys love him. He gets a fair bit of stick for how old he is but that comes to us all so I won't worry about that too much."

It has been 71 years since Warrington last won a league title and it is their first trip to Old Trafford for eight years.

In the Super League era, the Wire have now reached five Grand Finals, but are yet to cross the line and write their name on the trophy.

For Ben Currie, he is acutely aware of the gap between trophies, having been with the club during their four other visits - albeit he is yet to actually a appear in a Grand Final.

"It's hard not to know about it when you've got the opposite fans singing about it every week," he told BBC Radio Merseyside.

"Obviously it's tongue in cheek and it's fun for the fans to do that.

"We'd love to give our fans the opportunity to sing back to them but there's no added pressure from anyone from above in the club, from the coaching staff or from the senior players.

"Everyone wants it just the same as everyone does at Wakefield."

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

Wigan's O'Neill wins Man of Steel award

One member of the Warrington team who could make an impact is 18-year-old Ewan Irwin.

Since making his debut in 2025, Irwin has gone on to make 21 appearances this season, scoring six tries and kicking 82 goals.

Matty Ashton, who himself was a bright young prospect for the Wire not so long ago, spoke highly of his team-mate, who has the chance to become the youngest player to ever score in a Grand Final.

"You see him day in and day out, his work ethic, he's probably the best I've seen in a young lad [and] obviously I've been at the club for seven years," Ashton said of Irwin to BBC Radio Merseyside.

"The way he's willing to learn when he speaks to leaders like George [Williams], it's just great to see.

"He's just got that something, you can see it. Obviously I don't want to put too much pressure as he's my team-mate, but he'll go all the way and he's got a big chance to do something like that."

Warrington name a squad with just one change in their line-up.

Jordy Crowther comes into the squad, with Max Wood dropping out.

Wakefield, meanwhile, are unchanged following their dramatic semi-final win against Wigan Warriors.

Josh Rourke is once again named in their provisional squad as he continues his return from a knee injury sustained in August.

Warrington (from): Taylor-Wray, Thewlis, King, Hopoate, Ashton, Williams, Yates, Walker, Harrison, Stone, Currie, Powell, Byrne, Crowther, Irwin, Hayes, Bentley, Philbin, Lindop, Smith, Tanginoa.

Wakefield (from): Jowitt, Scott, Hall, Johnstone, Trueman, Lino, McMeeken, Smoothy, Rodwell, Tevaga, Pitts, Hamlin-Uele, Faatili, Smith, Vagana, Walmsley, Sinfield, Myers, Rourke, Lolesio, Lipowicz.

title: How Gordon became one of England's main men
description: Anthony Gordon has been England's in-form player since the World Cup knockout stage -  is the Barcelona forward now undroppable?
fullText:
Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Declan Rice, Jordan Pickford and now Anthony Gordon.

All have become guaranteed starters and reliable stars for England, with the Barcelona winger the latest to look, according to captain Kane, like one of the Three Lions' "main men".

Gordon was one of England's standout players at the World Cup and earned a big-money move to European giants Barca in the summer, while his good form has continued into his country's Nations League campaign.

He scored the opening goal in England's 2-0 win against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night, after also netting in a 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday.

In fact, the 25-year-old's England form has been building since the knockout stage of the World Cup began - his run of averaging a goal contribution every 69 minutes started with assisting both Kane's efforts in a 2-1 last-32 victory over DR Congo.

The former Newcastle player has scored three goals and provided three assists in his past six England matches, while he also won the penalty in England's dramatic last-16 victory over Mexico at Azteca Stadium.

And after a positive start in Spain, where he has already picked up five assists in La Liga, Gordon looks to be joining boss Thomas Tuchel's "undroppable" bracket.

Tuchel likes to give his players clarity on their role and makes clear who they are up against in the squad and for a starting position.

When asked whether Gordon is getting to be one of the first names on the team-sheet, he said: "He's getting there. He's defending his shirt, he's defending his position - an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain.

"He was very decisive [against the Czech Republic] and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult but the technique and finishing was excellent.

"He scored against Spain so he has decisive actions and he's defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he's a very important player."

Gordon linked up well with his former Newcastle team-mate Lewis Hall on England's left and combined with right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start for the Three Lions in nearly two years, for the opening goal.

Gordon said he had been "dying" to link up with Alexander-Arnold, who is also playing in Spain for Barcelona's rivals Real Madrid.

"It's a great compliment and it's great to play with him," Alexander-Arnold said of Gordon.

"I tried to get the ball, and try and see what the best play is and try and play forward and create something. And I was able to get the pass."

Captain and record goalscorer Kane is a guaranteed starter in England's biggest matches but the position to the left of Kane has been a problem area for the team, with no player able to make it their own.

Gordon looks to have secured that role and Kane said the winger is "showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England".

"His performances in the last couple of games have been some of his best that he has played in an England shirt," Kane said.

"I think he is just relishing putting the shirt on and being one of the main men in the team. He is an important player for us and he showed that during the World Cup."

It has not always been a straightforward route into the team for Gordon.

Marcus Rashford, Eberechi Eze, Phil Foden and Noni Madueke have all featured for England from the left in the past couple of years.

Gordon started to emerge as a clear option during Lee Carsley's time in interim charge, but said himself last October that he had only shown "50%" of what he can do for England.

Now that seems to be coming to fruition. Against the Czech Republic he attempted four shots, more than any England player and more than any of his team-mates against Spain too.

Gordon is ranked in at least the top four of England players for expected assists (0.9), expected goals (0.9), passes into the box (14), touches in the opposition box (29), chances created (eight), and shots on target (five), since the start of the World Cup knockout stage.

His importance is underlined by the fact he has contributed the same amount of goals and assists, six, as Bellingham since England faced DR Congo.

There has been an interesting subplot with Gordon and Rashford competing for a left-wing space for England and effectively Barcelona.

Rashford was on loan at Barcelona last season but they opted to not make his move permanent, instead he returned to Manchester United while the Catalan club splashed out £69m to sign Gordon from Newcastle.

Gordon has the ability to take on his full-back on the inside or beat them for pace on the outside before putting in a cross.

"People raised eyebrows when Anthony Gordon went to Barcelona for the money that he did and Marcus Rashford came back to Manchester United," former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"He has become a key part of the England team. There were certain games in the World Cup where he was substituted and he shouldn't have been - I think others should have come off instead of him.

"Gordon [when he is] full of confidence running at pace like he does, he can go either way and he's causing full-backs all kind of problems."

Gordon says that since his move to Spain he has changed people's perception of him being a player who is only quick and presses well, even if they are two of his best attributes.

"I always felt in England, people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with," Gordon told ITV.

"Only the players I play with ever seem to notice that. I think now I'm at Barcelona and I play a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are actually starting to take notice that I'm not just quick.

"In England, it was never really respected because people just see me as really quick and really aggressive.

"In Spain, they really appreciate my IQ and quality because at Barca, if you're not technical, if you're not smart, you're going to stand out like a sore thumb."

Tuchel is starting to build a team he thinks can challenge and win the Euros in 2028.

But first he wants to win the Nations League, and if England are to do that, it is likely Gordon will have played a huge part.

Impossible for England to find another Kane - Tuchel

Injured O'Reilly withdraws from England squad

title: Carse charged but remains available for England
description: Brydon Carse is charged by the Cricket Regulator over an incident outside a Derby nightclub but remains available for selection by England.
fullText:
Brydon Carse has been charged by the Cricket Regulator over an incident outside a Derby nightclub but remains available for selection by England.

Carse was arrested and then de-arrested in the early hours of 23 August. A subsequent investigation into allegations of an assault was closed by Derbyshire Police with no action taken against the 31-year-old.

On Friday, the Regulator confirmed the pace bowler has been charged with breaching the England and Wales Cricket Board's (ECB) professional conduct regulations.

"The matter will now be referred to the independent Cricket Discipline Panel for adjudication," said the Regulator. "As the process is ongoing, no further comment will be made."

Carse is alleged to have breached regulation 3.2, which states: "No participant may conduct themself in a manner, do any act or make any omission at any time which is improper or which may be prejudicial to the interests of cricket or which may bring the ECB, the game of cricket or any cricketer or group of cricketers into disrepute."

In the aftermath of the Derby controversy, Carse was dropped from the England squad to play Pakistan in the second Test at Lord's and has not been called up since. He has continued to play county cricket for Durham.

On Thursday, he was left out of the squad for the one-day tri-series in Pakistan later this month, with decisions around his inclusion understood to be taken on a tour-by-tour basis.

Responding to the Regulator's charge, an ECB statement said: "We are aware of the Cricket Regulator's decision to charge Brydon Carse. Brydon now has the opportunity to respond through the established process.

"As we do not wish to prejudge the outcome, it would not be appropriate for us to comment further."

Carse currently holds a two-year England central contract that expires in the autumn of 2027. The Regulator charge has not triggered any alteration to his England deal.

Last month, white-ball captain and Carse's close friend Harry Brook said he needed a period away from the England team.

"I'm very good mates with Carsey," Brook told BBC Sport. "I've spoken a lot with him. I think he just needs time away from the international scene.

"He's working on a few things behind the scenes and hopefully he'll be ready at some point in the future."

England are supporting Carse through the Regulator's process, though the player will be left to make his own response to the charge.

The Derby incident was another late-night drinking controversy in a year when England have been dogged by off-field problems.

As a result, Test captain Joe Root said he was "hacked off" and also addressed his team to remind them of their responsibilities.

White-ball coach Brendon McCullum said Carse would need to "get his house in order" before he returned to the England team.

And new Test coach Stephen Fleming said players will be expected to meet the "standards" of an England cricketer.

"We pick on runs and wickets primarily, but I think it's foolish not to also say there are standards that need to be set," said Fleming.

"You need to behave in accordance with your position. We're in a very privileged position, and it's understanding that privilege and what goes along with it. It can't be convenient. You can't be when it suits you to do the right things, then when you don't want it to suit you, not."

title: Sabalenka 'trying hard to be easier on myself'
description: Aryna Sabalenka says she is "trying so hard to be easier on myself" as she begins her China Open campaign with victory over Renata Zarazua.
fullText:
Aryna Sabalenka said she was "trying so hard to be easier on myself" as she began her China Open campaign with victory over Renata Zarazua.

World number two Sabalenka hit 11 aces and did not face a break point in a 6-1 6-3 victory over the Mexican.

The Belarusian needed just 63 minutes to win her first match since losing her world number one ranking and her US Open crown to Elena Rybakina in September.

The 28-year-old is bidding for her first title since completing the 'Sunshine Double' in March, when she won Indian Wells and the Miami Open back-to-back.

It has been a mixed year for Sabalenka by her high standards. She will finish without a Grand Slam trophy for the first time since 2022 and has often struggled to control her frustrations on court.

Asked about being so self-critical, Sabalenka said: "I think this is a good and a bad side of my personality, that I always ask and wait for more from myself.

"Sometimes it can drive me forward, but sometimes it can really drain my energy.

"Maybe this is something I have to finally learn. I'm really trying so hard sometimes to be easier on myself."

Sabalenka will face Czech 20-year-old Nikola Bartunkova - who came close to beating her at the Berlin Open in June - in the third round.

Top seed Rybakina begins her campaign at the WTA 1000 event on Saturday.

Earlier, Britain's Katie Boulter fell 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 to Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova, while French Open champion Mirra Andreeva recovered to beat Chinese wildcard Yuan Yue 3-6 6-0 6-0.

In the men's event, sixth seed Daniil Medvedev produced 12 aces to beat Spain's Pablo Carreno Busta 6-4 6-2.

British pair Julian Cash and Lloyd Glasspool advanced in the doubles, beating Russia's Andrey Rublev and Karen Khachanov 6-3 6-4.

Novak Djokovic progressed to the third round of the men's tournament with a 4-6 7-6 (7-2) 6-2 victory over China's Bu Yunchaokete.

The six-time champion, who has never lost in Beijing in 31 matches, was given a scare by Bu after he dropped the first set.

Djokovic needed a medical timeout after giving back a break in the second set, accepting a time violation as he fought to regain his breath between points.

The 39-year-old Serb then consulted the trainer, as he had in his first-round win over Nuno Borges, but he dominated the tie-break.

Djokovic found his rhythm in the decider as he won four games in a row sealing victory after two hours and 52 minutes with a backhand winner.

He will face either US Open champion Alexander Zverev of Germany or China's Shang Juncheng on Saturday for a spot in the quarter-finals.

title: Tuchel would never rule out players not in top flight
description: England boss Thomas Tuchel says he would "never rule out" selecting someone who is not playing in the top flight, should Manchester City be relegated.
fullText:
England boss Thomas Tuchel says he would "never rule out" selecting someone who is playing outside the top flight for their club, should Manchester City be relegated as punishment for breaching financial regulations.

On Tuesday, it was confirmed that City had been found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The club, which denies guilt, has appealed against the verdict, saying the ruling contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

The sanctions for City have not yet been decided but potential punishments include expulsion from the league, points deductions and fines.

The current England squad includes City players Elliot Anderson and Marc Guehi, while Nico O'Reilly was in the group until he left with an injury.

How Gordon became one of England's main men

England are preparing to play Croatia in the Nations League in Rijeka on Saturday (17:00 BST).

Speaking to the media on Friday, Tuchel said the City verdict was a "big subject" in the England camp.

Asked if he would select players not playing in the top flight, the manager said: "There is always a possibility.

"I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament.

"I will never rule out that because they don't play in the top flight in their country. We need to look at it case by case."

All 24 players in the current England squad play in top leagues for their clubs and it is very unusual for a player to represent the Three Lions if they are not in a top division.

However, James Trafford was in Tuchel squads in March and June 2025 while still in the Championship with Burnley, but he was an unused substitute on those occasions and did not win a full cap until he returned to Manchester City.

Goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was the last player to represent England while playing in the Championship, for West Brom in 2021, while Kalvin Phillips - then at Leeds - made his debut for England before he had played in the Premier League.

Asked about his players discussing the City verdict, Tuchel said: "We had some time off between the matches and it is a big subject. Everyone speaks about it, so there is no other voice needed

"I am glad to be not that voice. No-one needs my half knowledge on the topic.

"Of course, the players talk about it. City players talk about it. We talk with them but only briefly.

"They are ready to go tomorrow, that's what they show on the pitch and in camp. But of course, it's a big topic in the camp."
